papers_seen.author: Ponce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models across vision, language, speech, and other modalities. KD methods operate over multiple signals and protocols and are most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that also addresses data, architecture, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—from soft-target (logit) transfer to feature- and relational-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed and applied across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and objective design are aligned; persistent challenges include data scarcity, teacher–student architecture mismatch, transferred biases, and reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond simple soft-logit matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and hybrids with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on careful alignment of objectives, teacher/student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distributional failures. This review synthesizes methods, empirical patterns, limitations, and practical recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-capacity deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. Methods range from transferring soft labels to matching intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, synthesizing surrogate data for data-free distillation, and integrating distillation into federated and privacy-sensitive regimes. Empirical gains have been demonstrated across computer vision, generative modeling, graph learning, and natural language processing, while theoretical work and empirical studies highlight nuanced trade-offs related to regularization, sample selection, teacher quality, and heterogeneous/distributed data. Open challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, principled teacher-student design, and compression of generative and transformer models for real-world low-latency deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bolton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Model‑Compression Pipelines: Necessary, Versatile, and Bounded
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods that should be treated as a configurable core within integrated model‑compression pipelines. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains across modalities but is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on aligning distilled signals, teacher–student capacity and architectures, data strategies (including data‑free or privacy‑aware regimes), and complementary compression primitives. Effective deployment therefore requires task‑aware choices, safeguards for robustness and fairness, and continued work on principled theory and reliable distillation under limited or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional, and Integrative Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows KD can substantially reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving predictive quality when combined with appropriate design choices. However, KD is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on careful selection of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data regime and synthesis, optimization design, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degraded rare‑token behavior. Treating KD as a configurable core element of an integrated compression pipeline — combined with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, data strategies, and explicit safeguards — yields the most robust deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Central but Insufficient: A Task‑Aware, Pipeline‑Centric Position for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable set of techniques that reliably reduces inference cost by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, and speech tasks shows that carefully designed KD pipelines often recover most of teacher performance — and in some circumstances can even improve student generalization — but consistent success requires task‑aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the default, central component of model‑compression workflows while being explicitly integrated into broader, deployment‑aware pipelines that address teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, fairness/privacy risks, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core set of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, or privacy. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning internal features, attention maps, and layer correspondences; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture search. KD supports many practical settings — including data-limited, data-free, few-shot, federated, and cross-modal scenarios — but its effectiveness depends on choices such as which teacher signals to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases. Ongoing directions include principled theory for transfer objectives, robust and private distillation, and task-aware designs for structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, configurable family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger 'teacher' models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster 'student' models to meet latency, memory, energy, or privacy constraints. Modern KD extends far beyond simple logits matching: practitioners match intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals, or use contrastive and adversarial objectives; they apply online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data‑free protocols; and they combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is most effective when treated as a component within an integrated compression pipeline that is aligned to task objectives, teacher/student architectures, available data, and deployment constraints. Important limits remain — teacher–student capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, distribution shift, and scarce or private transfer data — which motivate task-aware design, data synthesis or privacy-preserving workflows, and careful evaluation prior to deployment.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques that transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and model size while often preserving most of the original performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline—choosing appropriate transfer targets, adapting objectives to student capacity and data regimes, and combining distillation with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections (including bias), data scarcity or privacy constraints, and difficulty preserving rare or structured behaviors require targeted mitigations, careful evaluation, and continued methodological and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. A wide variety of distillation objectives and protocols—ranging from logits and feature matching to ensemble, adversarial, self- and teacher-free methods—have been developed and successfully applied across machine translation, retrieval, speech, recommendation, vision, and multimodal tasks. KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data complexity, and alignment between teacher and student, and it can propagate teacher errors (especially on low-frequency phenomena) unless mitigated by targeted design choices. When combined with data-centric practices (filtering, augmentation), ensemble strategies, intermediate-layer alignment, or complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization), KD provides a robust, broadly applicable framework for achieving favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger systems. Across modalities and tasks—including classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and sequence prediction—distillation has been adapted to transfer ensemble knowledge, reduce computation and storage, improve generalization and fairness, enable private or federated deployment, and inject specialized inductive biases. While effective, distillation requires careful design choices (teacher quality, which examples to transfer, whether to use intermediate-layer alignment, robustness and privacy mechanisms) to avoid failure modes. This work argues that KD should be treated not just as a compression trick but as a unifying framework for controlled transfer of behaviors, and outlines empirical and theoretical findings that guide best practices for its application.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is now a central, broadly applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and functional behavior of larger teachers. The literature describes a rich taxonomy of KD objectives and protocols — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures — together with specialized strategies for online, multi-teacher, data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and acts as a regularizer, but success depends on task-aware choices: which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of teacher errors or low-frequency behaviors. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), curriculum and augmentation strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while enabling adaptation across tasks, domains, and modalities. When combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher engineering, pre-training of compact architectures, and input-side interventions (e.g., augmentation or data synthesis), KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss and can enable deployment under tight compute, latency, or privacy constraints. At the same time, KD is not a single recipe: success depends on optimization choices, teacher–student alignment, and dataset properties, which motivates tailored distillation objectives, data strategies, and evaluation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods provide practical routes to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. The literature has developed diverse approaches that transfer information via soft logits, intermediate features, attentional maps, channel-wise statistics, and online mutual learning; adaptations address task-specific compression, data-free or few-shot regimes, large-scale distributed training, and teacher-student co-optimization. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, and that selecting what, when, and how to transfer knowledge (e.g., logits vs. features, offline vs. online, task-aware filtering) is crucial to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A synthesis of methods, evidence, and practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical, multifaceted toolkit for transferring behavior from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students. The field unifies a set of objectives (soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online, self- and mutual-distillation, multi-teacher and teacher-annealed schedules), and data strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis, adversarial generation) that, when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), enable effective deployment across vision, language, generative modelling, and domain- and privacy-constrained settings. Empirical evidence demonstrates strong gains when distillation is matched to student capacity, teacher quality, and appropriate data/augmentation strategies, but persistent challenges remain in data-scarce, privacy-sensitive, domain-shift, and heterogeneous-architecture regimes.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Pragmatic, Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, distillation can preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployments with constrained compute, memory, latency, and privacy requirements. However, its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints (e.g., robustness, heterogeneity, data availability). When applied thoughtfully—using feature-based objectives, ensemble or adversarial strategies, data augmentation or data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression—KD reliably delivers practical trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted framework for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while retaining task performance. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and across multiple training regimes (offline teacher→student, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when paired with appropriate teacher–student design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, but key limitations remain around data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, transfer of undesirable behaviors, and insufficient theoretical understanding of what to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Potts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Tool Best Used in Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD consistently improves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when adapted to task and deployment constraints, but it is not a standalone solution: reliable compression requires attention to what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical use of KD therefore treats it as a configurable core of a broader, context‑aware model‑compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, a diverse toolbox of distillation targets, training protocols, and data strategies has been developed. Practical deployment typically treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) while attending to data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and risks such as transferred bias and degraded behavior on rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Leon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Integrated Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, versatile set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across modalities. Empirical evidence shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its reliability is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime, and the chosen distillation targets and protocol determine outcomes. For robust, deployment-ready compression, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and fairness/privacy safeguards—rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students, but it must be applied conditionally and integrated with task‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities when teacher quality, student capacity, distilled signals, and data regimes are aligned; however, known failure modes (teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena) require targeted remedies and validation for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language processing. KD encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and variants such as multi‑teacher, online, self‑distillation, and data‑ or privacy‑aware protocols. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and task‑aware training—to match deployment constraints while mitigating failure modes like capacity mismatch, transferred bias, distribution shift, and degraded handling of low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit and combined with complementary compression methods, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. However, its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy; it must be applied conditionally with safeguards against error and bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, more efficient students while preserving predictive behavior and, in many cases, improving deployment properties such as latency, memory use, privacy, and robustness. The field has expanded from matching teacher logits to a broad set of signals and workflows — internal feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free generation, curriculum and selective-sample protocols, meta- and online-teaching schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows that what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to align teacher and student (layer mapping, projectors), and which data to use (authentic, distilled, augmented, or synthetic) materially affect student outcomes. Practical deployments require task-aware design: align signals to student capacity, mitigate teacher error propagation, handle low-resource or privacy-constrained settings, and combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Remaining challenges include principled theory for which teacher signals are most informative across tasks, reliable transfer under data heterogeneity and domain shift, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically supported approach for producing compact, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods — including soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self-distillation, and data-free or adversarial synthesis — enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. The effectiveness of KD is strongly context dependent: it hinges on what signals are transferred, teacher–student design and capacity alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and integration with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. Remaining research and engineering challenges include robust and privacy-preserving distillation under data scarcity, improved methods for heterogeneous teacher–student mappings, and methods to avoid propagating teacher biases or damaging long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Burns
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for transferring behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD produces large practical gains when it is treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—and when practitioners attend to teacher–student capacity, data regime, and optimization design. KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with low-frequency phenomena, and fail under data scarcity or severe teacher–student mismatch. Therefore the recommended position is to adopt KD as the default first-line compression strategy, but to explicitly pair it with complementary methods and safeguards tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger or multi-modal models to smaller or specialized models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, and improve robustness or fairness. Across computer vision, natural language processing, speech, recommender systems, graph learning, generative modelling, and multimodal tasks, a broad set of mechanisms—soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and ensemble methods, online/peer-distillation, and task- or domain-specific adaptations—have been developed. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, accelerate training or inference, improve small-model self-supervised learning, and enable modality transfer, while theoretical and empirical analyses highlight factors that govern success: student capacity, teacher imperfection, data complexity, data augmentation, and bias-variance tradeoffs. Open challenges remain in principled theory, privacy-preserving and fairness-aware distillation, and extending distillation reliably to generative and highly structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applied family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals) and through diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online co‑distillation, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, and data‑ or privacy‑aware variants). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD is context dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and selection (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of transferred biases, low-frequency or out-of-distribution failures, and privacy concerns. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core component embedded in an integrated compression pipeline alongside complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining and curriculum methods).

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) supervision to representation- and layer-wise alignment—and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-augmentation or curriculum strategies. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generative models, and retrieval shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy and can add benefits such as improved generalization or interpretability when applied carefully. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, optimization choices, and explicit handling of teacher biases and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline, chosen and tuned to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and often indispensable method for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its objectives, data strategies, and student architectures are chosen with task and deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of transferred errors, biases, and rare-case failures. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be applied as a configurable, task-aware element of an integrated compression pipeline that also leverages representation-aware objectives, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary architecture-aware transformations.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential Tool for Practical Deep Learning — Potentials, Pitfalls, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have matured into indispensable tools for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained, privacy-sensitive, and latency-critical environments. Across modalities—vision, language, speech, and generation—KD enables smaller or heterogeneous models to approach teacher performance, improves interpretability in specific settings, and reduces communication costs in distributed learning. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, suffer under data heterogeneity, and interact subtly with training practices. Careful choices—selective sample usage, multi- or self-distillation, architectural adapters, annealing strategies, and privacy-aware generative replay—help realize KD's benefits while mitigating its limitations. This paper synthesizes evidence from applied and theoretical work to argue that KD should be treated as a central engineering primitive, accompanied by the practices needed for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Context‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD consistently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs when applied thoughtfully, but its benefits are conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and architecture alignment. Best practice treats KD as the central component of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and explicit mitigations for failure modes such as propagated bias, distribution shift, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied, practical framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. KD encompasses diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distributional failures.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are no longer just ways to reduce parameter counts; when designed thoughtfully they preserve or even improve task performance, domain robustness, and privacy while enabling real-time deployment. Effective distillation requires going beyond matching output probabilities: transferring internal representations, using task- and domain-aware selection of teacher signals, leveraging ensemble or adversarial schemes when appropriate, and adopting data-aware or data-free augmentation techniques. In application domains from NLP to vision, multi-modal systems, and graph learning, tailored distillation strategies yield substantial speedups and parameter reductions with minimal loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy. This paper synthesizes evidence across diverse recent works to advocate a principled, task-centered approach to distillation and compression.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Methods vary by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), by how teachers and students are arranged (offline, online, ensemble, self-distillation), and by how distillation is integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free regimes). KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can improve robustness or generalization in some settings, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful handling of bias, distribution shift, and privacy considerations.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models by transferring behavior from larger teacher models. When used as a configurable, task- and deployment-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline, KD routinely reduces latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Its practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives; persistent challenges include bias transfer, handling low-frequency phenomena, distribution shift, and automating signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, KD spans logit/soft-target matching, intermediate- representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or synthesized-data protocols. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables substantial efficiency gains, but its effectiveness is context-dependent and benefits from careful, task-aware choices about signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Key limitations include optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, degradation on low-frequency or long-tail phenomena, and sensitivity to distribution shift; proposed remedies include multi-signal objectives, augmentation and synthesized data, teacher scheduling, and combining KD with other compression and design techniques. Open research directions center on theoretical understanding, robust and privacy-aware distillation under limited or mismatched data, automated teacher/student co-design, and principled mitigation of fairness and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger or ensemble teachers. It supports a wide range of objectives—logit-level transfer, feature- and representation-level matching, relational and adversarial objectives, and many-to-many layer mappings—and is applicable across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) and settings (offline, online, data-free, federated, multi-teacher). When combined with careful teacher-student co-design, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while also serving secondary goals such as interpretability or robustness. KD is powerful but not automatic: success depends on matching objectives to tasks, mitigating teacher-induced errors or biases, and addressing optimization and data-distribution challenges.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or specialized models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teachers. When integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and objective design, and it raises open challenges in robustness, privacy, and automatic student design.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: An Indispensable but Context‑Dependent Toolbox
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to task constraints, data regimes, and student capacity, KD reliably produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD transfers teacher imperfections and faces limits (data mismatch, capacity gaps, low-frequency behavior), so it must be applied as a principled, task-aware set of techniques combined with complementary compression practices.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models. A rich set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, contrastive and adversarial objectives) and protocols (offline, online, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free, privacy‑aware) has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative modeling. Practical effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of data, and integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, distilling under data or privacy constraints, mitigating transferred biases and degraded rare-event behavior, and designing principled layer-to-layer mappings and data‑efficient protocols.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD has been adapted across logits-, feature-, and relation-level objectives, combined with complementary compression primitives, and applied in specialized settings (federated, data-free, recommender, and generative). Its practical value is substantial, but realizing that value requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mendez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade the field has diversified well beyond simple logits matching to include intermediate-feature and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, data-free or generator-based approaches, and task-aware engineering such as layer mapping and projector modules. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows that KD can produce substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often retaining much of a teacher’s performance; achieving reliable results requires careful choice of distillation signals, alignment between teacher and student, and integration with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. Important open problems remain around principled design, robust transfer under data scarcity and distribution shift, and mitigation of transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Herman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Evidence, Methods, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, and multimodal tasks shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing parameters, latency, and memory. Success is conditional: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of transferred signals, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies rather than as a one-shot cure.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Model Compression with Practical Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated family of techniques that enables production of compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and teacher-student design are matched to deployment constraints, but it is not a turnkey remedy: careful method selection and safeguards are required to avoid capacity mismatch, optimization failure modes, and transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multifaceted Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to map teacher and student layers, and whether to synthesize or reweight data—KD reliably enables latency-, memory-, and privacy-aware deployment across vision, language, generative, and structured tasks. However, its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, and data availability; therefore best practice combines task-aware distillation objectives with complementary compression techniques and safeguards against transferred errors and biases.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while attempting to preserve teacher performance. Work in KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft labels), aligning internal representations and features, adversarial or data-free sample synthesis, architecture search and task-adaptive compression, privacy-aware and federated settings, and domain- or task-specific adaptations. Empirical results show KD can yield dramatic reductions in size and compute with modest drops (or even gains) in downstream performance across speech, vision, and NLP tasks, but success depends on what is distilled (outputs versus internal features), optimization and dataset choices, and problem-specific design choices. The literature also identifies limitations and failure modes—optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and privacy constraints—that have motivated specialized protocols and theory. This synthesis summarizes the principal approaches, mechanistic explanations, representative empirical outcomes, and practical considerations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Compton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training protocols, and it is most effective when treated as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies. While KD can recover much of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success is context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and selection, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Realizing KD's full potential requires task-aware engineering, complementary compression primitives, and focused research on theoretical foundations and robust, privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. By transferring predictive behavior or internal representations, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training, KD forms an essential, configurable component of modern compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language processing. KD encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and variants such as multi‑teacher, online, self‑distillation, and data‑ or privacy‑aware protocols. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and task‑aware training—to match deployment constraints while mitigating failure modes like capacity mismatch, transferred bias, distribution shift, and degraded handling of low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Serrano
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal settings, KD methods — from soft‑target (logit) matching to feature- and relation-level objectives, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑free or privacy‑aware protocols — consistently improve accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with task‑aware design and complementary compression techniques. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires careful attention to teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture alignment, what signals are transferred and how layers are mapped, data availability or synthesis strategies, and interventions to mitigate bias, rare‑token degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central and Practical — but Context‑Dependent — Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary teacher models into compact students. KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities when paired with task‑aware choices of distilled targets, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives; however, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit safeguards against transferred artifacts and distributional mismatch. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a plug‑and‑play silver bullet.
