papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesized Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal information. A broad toolbox of distillation targets and protocols has emerged—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher schemes—and these are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, generative models, and federated settings, yielding large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when design choices are task- and architecture-aware. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability in optimization; practical remedies emphasize task-aware signal selection, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving protocols. This review synthesizes empirical patterns, common mechanisms, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Singleton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows KD methods often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. However, KD exhibits well-documented failure modes—capacity and architecture mismatch, transfer of teacher errors and biases, degraded long-tail behavior, and sensitivity to data regimes—that require complementary algorithmic and pipeline-level remedies. Treating KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression strategy (combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and careful data or privacy protocols) is the most reliable path to practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Bolton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Model‑Compression Pipelines: Necessary, Versatile, and Bounded
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods that should be treated as a configurable core within integrated model‑compression pipelines. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains across modalities but is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on aligning distilled signals, teacher–student capacity and architectures, data strategies (including data‑free or privacy‑aware regimes), and complementary compression primitives. Effective deployment therefore requires task‑aware choices, safeguards for robustness and fairness, and continued work on principled theory and reliable distillation under limited or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core technique for producing compact, efficient models and for enabling cross-model, cross-modal, and privacy-sensitive transfer in deep learning and NLP. KD can be implemented at the logit, feature, and layer levels, and extended to ensemble teachers, data-free scenarios, federated settings, and task-adaptive architecture search. While KD often yields large efficiency gains with small accuracy loss, its effectiveness depends on data properties, teacher–student alignment, and training choices; addressing limitations such as data heterogeneity, low-frequency token degradation, and mismatched inputs requires tailored methods (e.g., feature mimicking, teacher adaptation, multi-teacher weighting, and specialized divergences). Building on empirical and methodological work across modalities, I argue that KD should be treated as a versatile, application-driven toolkit rather than a single recipe, and that future progress will come from combining representational-level distillation, teacher-aware training, and methods that reduce reliance on original training data.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—classification, detection, generation, retrieval, recommendation, graph learning, and language modeling—KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices and latency-sensitive pipelines. However, maximizing benefits requires addressing teacher-student capacity gaps, computational cost of teacher supervision, and task-specific information selection; a variety of methodological extensions (multi-teacher schedules, feature/projector design, adversarial or decision-boundary driven samples, layer- and task-aware filtering, self-distillation, and meta-learned teachers) have been developed to meet these needs. When combined appropriately with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), distillation yields state-of-the-art trade-offs for real applications.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer behavior or internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to reduce latency, memory, and communication costs while retaining performance. Across modalities, researchers have developed logits-based supervision, feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and architecture-aware compression. These methods are applied to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, federated and privacy-sensitive settings, domain adaptation, generative-model compression, and improved fairness or robustness when combined with task-aware design. Despite strong empirical gains, important challenges remain in handling distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous architectures, and data-scarce or data-free scenarios. Emerging directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, joint optimization with pruning and NAS, federated/distilled learning across heterogeneous devices, and cross-modal distillation for generative and segmentation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques — spanning soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and teacher-aware or multi-teacher strategies — repeatedly enable large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task and data properties, teacher–student alignment, optimization, and deployment constraints, and it works best when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthetic Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical set of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. The approach has diversified beyond simple logits-matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multiple training protocols (offline, online, self-, multi-teacher, and data-free), and task-aware adaptations such as layer mapping, projector modules, and synthetic-data strategies. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, graph, and multimodal tasks demonstrates that KD can deliver substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining most of a teacher’s performance; success in practice requires careful matching of distillation signals, attention to teacher–student alignment, and integration with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD routinely reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core element within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and task-aware data strategies—and couples it with explicit measures to mitigate bias, robustness failures, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals and training protocols, and they are most effective when integrated with task‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. KD routinely enables large efficiency gains but requires careful handling of teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and known failure modes for robust, deployable compression.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression trick into a broad set of techniques that enable efficient deployment, cross-modal transfer, federated and privacy-preserving learning, and improved generalization across domains. Empirical results across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs) show that KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining most of the teacher performance. However, the success of KD depends on careful choices — teacher quality, what to distill (outputs, features, internal representations), data availability and augmentation, and the loss or alignment mechanism — and recent work proposes multiple refinements (multi-teacher schemes, adversarial critics, projector modules, teacher-free variants) that mitigate known failure modes. The balance of empirical evidence and theoretical analyses indicates that KD is both practically indispensable for many compression tasks and a fertile area for research on how knowledge should be measured, transferred, and regularized.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of task performance. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit matching into a broad set of targets and protocols—soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention/relational objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and multi- or self-distillation—frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and alignment of data (or synthetic alternatives), and careful design of objectives and pipelines. Remaining practical limits include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints; current remedies emphasize task-aware objective design, multi-signal supervision, teacher adaptation, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate-feature matching, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-free or generator-driven protocols—routinely recover a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression primitives. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; consequently KD is most reliable when used as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, pretraining, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mendez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. Over the past decade the field has diversified well beyond simple logits matching to include intermediate-feature and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, data-free or generator-based approaches, and task-aware engineering such as layer mapping and projector modules. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows that KD can produce substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often retaining much of a teacher’s performance; achieving reliable results requires careful choice of distillation signals, alignment between teacher and student, and integration with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. Important open problems remain around principled design, robust transfer under data scarcity and distribution shift, and mitigation of transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide a practical path to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Across vision and language, researchers have explored teacher-student training, intermediate-layer alignment, data- and label-space manipulations, data-free or few-shot settings, and architecture-aware compression. These techniques can preserve much of a teacher's performance while yielding smaller, faster models, and they can be combined with pruning, architecture search, or ensemble compression. KD also intersects with concerns about fairness, generalization, and privacy, and its effectiveness depends on design choices such as the form of distilled targets, data augmentation, and the match between teacher, student, and task.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable set of techniques that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to task and data constraints, KD unlocks deployment on latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained platforms while supporting modalities from language to vision and multimodal systems. However, KD is not automatic: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, rare-token degradation) are required for responsible, robust outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, federated) together with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search, module replacement) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD’s success is context-dependent: outcomes depend on the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit measures to mitigate bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and applying task- and data-aware design choices yields the most reliable practical results.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central strategies for deploying large deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of methods—ranging from soft-label distillation, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer mapping, adversarial and data-free techniques, to task-adaptive architecture search and meta-learning of teachers—have been proposed to transfer performance from bulky teachers to compact students. These approaches are applied across domains including vision, language, multi-modal systems, recommender systems, and domain-specific NLP, and they trade off fidelity to the teacher, generalization, and computational efficiency. Empirical results show that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while yielding substantial speedups and memory reductions, and in some settings can even improve fairness, robustness, or downstream generalization. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and representations across teacher and student, coping with absent or private training data, and automatically selecting what and how to transfer for specific tasks and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Context‑Aware, and Best Used Within Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD reduces inference cost and memory footprint and enables deployment in latency-, compute-, and privacy-constrained environments. Its many variants—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-/self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—have shown broad empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Despite this success, KD’s effectiveness is strongly context-dependent: it requires careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and fidelity, and targeted mitigation of failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, degraded rare-case behavior, and fairness or privacy concerns. Treating KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline (combining pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies) yields the most reliable results for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with task‑aware design, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods; however, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, biases, and low‑frequency failures. Treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to produce deployable systems under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of KD objectives and training regimes—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate feature and relation-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) enables substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. KD�s practical success is conditional on task-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher�student alignment, data availability and augmentation, and explicit handling of bias, low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving functionality. Beyond simple size reduction, distillation enables device deployment, privacy-preserving releases, latency reduction, ensemble compression, improved low-precision accuracy, and better generalization when combined with complementary techniques. Successful deployment requires matching distillation method to problem structure (e.g., graphs, vision-language, transformers), addressing teacher-induced biases, and adopting strategies such as data-free synthesis, task-aware layer selection, relational objectives, and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely used family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods have expanded from simple logits-matching to include feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols, and many-to-many teacher–student mappings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability or synthesis. KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Stanley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. KD spans matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free protocols, and multi- or online-teacher schemes. Empirical work shows KD typically recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can interact positively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and explicit mitigation of bias, distribution shift, and low-frequency failures. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically effective approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving most of a teacher's performance—but it is context dependent, requiring careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, privacy, and deployment constraints. Treated as the configurable core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware data strategies), KD enables deployable models for latency- and resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings; however, practitioners must explicitly address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, low-frequency errors, and propagated biases.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and training protocols, distillation operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful objective and optimization design; important limitations include teacher error propagation, impaired modeling of low-frequency phenomena, and distribution-shift vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical framework for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline/online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free/federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) allows practitioners to recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance across modalities when teacher–student compatibility, data strategy, and optimization design are carefully managed. KD is most reliable when embedded in a task‑aware compression pipeline that attends to data availability, teacher quality, student capacity, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; persistent challenges include principled theory for diverse objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD provides multiple transfer signals and training protocols that, when combined with complementary compression techniques, enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness is highly context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and objective design shape outcomes and failure modes. Practical use emphasizes configurable pipelines that integrate distillation with data strategies and other compression primitives while addressing robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile framework that enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component—combining logits, intermediate-feature matching, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and privacy-aware techniques—distillation supports deployment across modalities and constrained devices. However, KD is not automatic: it propagates some teacher errors, can lose low-frequency or structured information, and requires careful design choices (teacher selection, objective weighting, data strategy). A principled practice that matches the distillation objective to the task, augments or tailors distillation data, and applies privacy- or domain-aware protocols yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Schmitt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Configurable Core for Practical Model Compression with Explicit Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven approach for producing compact models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure when tailored to the task, signals, and deployment constraints, but it has clear limits: teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and difficulty preserving low-frequency behaviors. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives, careful layer mapping, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet real-world deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Foundational, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as Part of an Integrated Compression Toolkit
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful set of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD variants—from logits and feature matching to self-, multi-teacher, and data-free protocols—have been shown to reduce model size and latency while often retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, generative, and detection tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, what is transferred, and interactions with other training practices. To realize KD’s practical value one should design distillation around task objectives and deployment constraints and combine it with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Vang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), supports online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free regimes, and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its empirical success spans vision, language, speech, retrieval and multimodal generation, but outcomes are context‑dependent: they depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or public data), and task‑aware objective design. Documented failure modes include capacity and optimization mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, difficulty preserving low‑frequency phenomena and distributional mismatch. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and emphasizes careful signal selection, data and curriculum strategies, and targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of objectives (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection (or synthesis), and task‑aware design choices. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled methods for heterogeneous architectures and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Kline
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into compact student models. The literature provides a rich toolbox—output-level (soft targets), intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants such as multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, data‑free and meta‑learning approaches. Empirical and conceptual work agrees that KD is most effective when adapted to task constraints, student capacity, and data availability and when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design).

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. Empirical results across vision, language, retrieval, detection, generative models, and distributed settings show KD can close much of the performance gap between large and compact models, but best outcomes require tailoring what and how knowledge is transferred and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques and domain-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are indispensable for moving state-of-the-art deep models from research to real-world deployment. By transferring predictive behavior, representations, or relational structure from larger or specialized teachers to smaller students, KD enables faster inference, smaller footprints, better generalization across domains, privacy-preserving sharing, and adaptation to heterogeneous hardware and data constraints. Realizing these benefits in practice requires combining algorithmic advances (multi-teacher regimes, curriculum and projector design, augmentation and adversarial synthesis), systems thinking (federated and client-inclusive protocols), and attention to pitfalls (mismatched objectives, erased class relations). Together, the literature shows KD is not a niche trick but a broad, flexible toolkit for addressing latency, capacity, distribution shift, privacy, and interpretability in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models by transferring information from larger or specialized models. It supports a broad range of objectives beyond raw compression—improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, supporting privacy-aware or federated workflows, and permitting deployment on constrained hardware. KD methods range from simple soft-label matching to richer transfers of intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive structure. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, alignment between teacher and student, data availability and distribution, and the choice of signals and losses. When applied with attention to these constraints and combined sensibly with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), KD is a practical foundational technique for real-world model compression in vision, language, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central Tool, Context-Aware Integration
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD variants—matching logits, imitating intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher or self-distillation regimes, and supporting data-free or privacy-aware setups—have demonstrated broad applicability across vision, speech, language, retrieval, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and fidelity of distillation data, and task-specific needs. Best outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful layer and feature alignment, and data- or task-aware strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. KD has been shown to work across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It can also be combined with data augmentation, adversarial schemes, online or teacher-free training, and architecture-aware adaptations to meet deployment constraints. KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, alignment of inputs and architectures, student capacity, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. When used as part of a task-aware compression pipeline that addresses these issues, KD delivers substantial practical benefits for latency- and resource-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: The Centrality and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. Beyond reducing parameter counts and inference latency, distillation enables transferring inductive biases, protecting privacy in federated settings, enabling few- and zero-shot compression, and supporting task-adaptive and automated compression workflows. However, distillation is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity, teacher–student mismatch, and redundant teacher representations can limit gains. Best practice combines representation-level and layer-aware techniques, multi-teacher or teacher-free strategies where appropriate, and task-aware selection of distilled information to maximize compressed-model utility.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Advocated Conditional-First Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, broadly applicable set of techniques that enable compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment in vision, language, speech, and multimodal systems. KD reliably reduces latency, memory, and compute requirements while often preserving much of a teacher model’s performance, but its success is conditional: on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. As a result, KD should be treated as a primary engineering primitive for compression that must be combined with task- and deployment-aware design, complementary compression techniques, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness. Future progress requires better theoretical understanding of transferable signals, automated teacher–student alignment, and methods that address privacy, distribution shift, and low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Versatile, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable paradigm for producing smaller, deployable models from larger teachers. KD provides many transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, contrastive objectives, and synthetic/data‑free protocols) and is effective across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks when paired with task- and capacity-aware design. However, KD has predictable failure modes—propagation of teacher errors and biases, capacity and distribution mismatches, difficulty preserving low-frequency or structured behaviors, and data/privacy constraints—that limit its reliability as a sole compression method. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), explicit teacher–student alignment, targeted data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation/mitigation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Component of Integrated Model Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Rather than a standalone cure, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that aligns distilled signals, teacher–student capacity, and data strategy, and that combines distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Responsible deployment requires addressing known failure modes—data scarcity and distribution shift, capacity mismatch, degraded low-frequency behavior, and bias/privacy risks—through targeted remedies and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practically driven toolbox for transferring performance from large teacher models to smaller student models across modalities and tasks. Methods span soft-label supervision, feature- and layer-wise imitation, adversarial and ensemble-based transfer, data- and privacy-aware protocols, and integration with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but gains depend strongly on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, domain shift, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior, representations, or relational structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and online/self- or multi-teacher protocols—are widely used across vision, language, speech, multimodal and federated settings. When combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, effectiveness is context-dependent: KD success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and explicit mitigation of propagated biases, low-frequency failures, and distribution shift. Continued progress requires principled theory, robust data- and privacy-aware distillation, automated teacher–student co-design, and practical safeguards for fairness and rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central and Practical — but Context‑Dependent — Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary teacher models into compact students. KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities when paired with task‑aware choices of distilled targets, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives; however, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit safeguards against transferred artifacts and distributional mismatch. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a plug‑and‑play silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), adapts to data-limited and privacy‑sensitive settings, and interoperates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its empirical strengths make KD a first‑line approach for many deployment problems, but reliable, production‑grade compression requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection or synthesis, capacity matching, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance and functionality of larger teacher models. KD is highly versatile—operating at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and generative models). However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are no longer just ways to reduce parameter counts; when designed thoughtfully they preserve or even improve task performance, domain robustness, and privacy while enabling real-time deployment. Effective distillation requires going beyond matching output probabilities: transferring internal representations, using task- and domain-aware selection of teacher signals, leveraging ensemble or adversarial schemes when appropriate, and adopting data-aware or data-free augmentation techniques. In application domains from NLP to vision, multi-modal systems, and graph learning, tailored distillation strategies yield substantial speedups and parameter reductions with minimal loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy. This paper synthesizes evidence across diverse recent works to advocate a principled, task-centered approach to distillation and compression.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Engine for Practical Model Compression — Powerful but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practically proven approach for transferring capabilities from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce latency, memory use, and energy while preserving much of task performance. KD excels when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student alignment, and appropriate data strategies; however, it is not a universal remedy. Reliable deployment requires treating KD as a configurable component of integrated compression pipelines with explicit provisions for teacher quality, data scarcity, distribution shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have matured into a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across computer vision, NLP, multimodal systems, federated settings, and generative models, researchers have combined soft-label (logit) distillation, intermediate feature/hint transfer, architecture transformation, quantization, pruning, and automated search to achieve significant reductions in memory, computation, or communication while largely preserving accuracy. Empirical work demonstrates that distillation can enable high-quality low-precision models, speed up inference and training, unify heterogeneous models without shared data, and make distributed learning more communication- and privacy-efficient. The field continues to refine when and what knowledge to transfer (e.g., logits vs. features vs. attention), how to handle multiple or unreliable teachers, how to design student-friendly teachers, and how to integrate distillation with other compression methods such as pruning and search.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger, more accurate, or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Over the past decade KD has broadened from matching teacher output probabilities to a diverse set of objectives that include internal representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and online or self-distillation schedules. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training pipelines, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transferred errors, biases, and distributional brittleness.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational constraints), can be adapted to data‑limited and data‑free regimes, and combines productively with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, reliable deployment requires task‑aware design: selecting appropriate distillation objectives, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, addressing data regimes and privacy constraints, and mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare or low‑frequency phenomena. Treated as a configurable core of compression pipelines and paired with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices, KD enables practical, deployable model compression across modalities and settings.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Strengths, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core set of techniques for transferring information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Through objectives that match outputs, internal representations, or relational structure, KD enables reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often retaining much of teacher performance. The approach has been extended into many variants—feature- and layer-level alignment, attention- or projector-based mappings, multi-teacher and online schemes, data‑free and privacy-aware protocols, curriculum and adversarial sample strategies—and is applied across classification, retrieval, translation, evaluation metrics, and graph learning. Practical deployment requires addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, data and distributional constraints, and potential transfer of teacher artifacts; combining KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware distillation design produces the best results. Open directions center on principled selection of what to distill, robust distillation under data heterogeneity or privacy constraints, and automated, deployment-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Chang

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller student models. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, structured signals) and combines naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. Effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and optimization design; addressing these practical dimensions is central to reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-representation and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free protocols; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely produces substantial efficiency gains while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance when the distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind. Practical deployment requires explicit attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of bias, robustness, and privacy risks. Important open problems remain in principled theory, robust transfer under distribution shift and scarce data, and preserving low-frequency or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Goodman

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods include output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self- and multi-teacher protocols, and data‑free or privacy-aware synthesis. When combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely produces substantial reductions in latency, memory, and parameter footprint while retaining much of teacher performance. The effectiveness of KD is highly context dependent: it relies on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis strategies, and explicit treatment of robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include principled teacher–student design, reliable distillation under data scarcity and distribution shift, mitigation of bias transfer, and automation of distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of broader compression pipelines and adopts safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical, flexible approach to compressing large neural models into resource-efficient students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks — from language and retrieval to vision, generation, and graph learning — distillation techniques enable trade-offs between accuracy, compute, and memory that make deployment feasible on constrained hardware. However, the effectiveness of distillation depends strongly on the distillation objective, the information transferred (probabilities, internal representations, or structured signals), availability of original data, and care to avoid transferring undesirable teacher properties. When combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, architecture search, low-precision training, or curriculum strategies), distillation can yield compact models that approach or sometimes even exceed teacher performance while meeting practical latency and size constraints.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely adopted set of techniques that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Best results come when distillation is configured to the task—choosing appropriate signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies. KD is therefore a core, configurable element of effective compression pipelines, but it is not by itself a universal cure: careful engineering and safeguards are required to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, fairness, robustness, and preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors.
