papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Fuentes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When integrated with complementary compression techniques and adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints, distillation routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Success requires careful selection of distillation signals, alignment between teacher and student, appropriate data or synthetic examples, and explicit safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness. Distillation should therefore be treated as a configurable, central component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a plug‑and‑play solution.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, latency, and communication while attempting to preserve task performance. KD methods include matching output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture/behavior-aware design. Empirical evidence across modalities shows KD often recovers a substantial fraction of teacher performance and enables real-world deployment, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the data used for distillation, and strategies for mitigating transferred errors, distribution shift, privacy risks, and degraded performance on low-frequency or minority behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Willis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, multimodal, and structured tasks. The literature frames KD as a configurable toolkit of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and engineering integrations (projectors, curriculum scheduling, data augmentation, architecture search, pruning, quantization). KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve robustness or generalization when applied with task-aware design, but its success is context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of teacher biases, low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Practical systems therefore treat KD as a central component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone, universal recipe.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft targets/logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals, contrastive or adversarial objectives) and in varied protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and federated regimes). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal domains shows KD frequently restores a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends critically on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategy, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as teacher-error propagation, bias transfer, and degraded low‑frequency behaviour. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and careful data/objective choices—to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or adapts large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, generative models, and domain- or privacy-constrained settings, a diverse toolbox has been developed—soft-label supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations (e.g., pruning, layer skipping, NAS). Empirical results show that appropriately designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments, while practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and optimization design. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, privacy-and-fairness-aware protocols, and extending KD to complex generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for transferring behavior and representations from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of a teacher's performance. Its practical value emerges when KD is used as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines that also employ pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies. At the same time, KD is not sufficient by itself: success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distillation signals, and careful handling of data, bias, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is most effective when treated as a central element of a broader compression portfolio that includes architecture-aware design, pre-training, pruning/quantization, and privacy- or data-aware protocols. Practical deployment benefits from careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align teacher and student, and when to apply auxiliary methods; remaining challenges include robustness under distributional shift, teacher imperfections, low-frequency token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Methods vary by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), by how teachers and students are arranged (offline, online, ensemble, self-distillation), and by how distillation is integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free regimes). KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can improve robustness or generalization in some settings, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful handling of bias, distribution shift, and privacy considerations.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and flexible family of methods that enables deployment of large models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations into smaller students. KD routinely delivers large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and the choice of signals to transfer. For robust, production‑grade compression KD should be treated as the central building block of an integrated, task‑aware pipeline that combines representational distillation, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), while explicitly mitigating bias transfer, low‑frequency degradation, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Mann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. The literature has expanded KD beyond simple soft-target matching to include representation- and structure-level objectives, a variety of training schedules (offline, online, self-distillation, data-free), and many task- and architecture-aware adaptations. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves most of teacher performance and sometimes improves robustness or calibration, but outcomes are sensitive to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the data available for distillation, and the particular signals chosen for transfer. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture choices—and emphasizes task-aware design, data strategies, and safeguards against transferred biases or degraded low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional, and Integrative Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential method for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases that yield substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy. However, KD has concrete failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias transfer, and distribution shift—that limit its effectiveness when used alone. The strongest, most reliable outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable core of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that combines careful teacher engineering, targeted distillation signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal systems, and specialized domains such as healthcare and novel-view synthesis, KD yields large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher performance when applied with task-aware design choices. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what information is transferred (logits, features, relational structure), the availability and nature of data, teacher quality and design, and careful integration with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Pragmatic deployment requires attention to robustness, bias propagation, data scarcity, and domain mismatch, and benefits most from combining KD with task- and hardware-aware practices.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑aware Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical framework for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across speech, vision, translation, and evaluation metrics, KD variants (soft labels, feature/attention matching, adversarial and data-free schemes, and self‑distillation) have enabled deployable models under latency, memory, privacy, and communication constraints. KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with distribution or capacity mismatch, and require task‑aware adaptations. When used as part of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline—combining layer‑wise alignment, pretraining, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, or synthetic data generation—KD reliably yields practical tradeoffs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of broader compression pipelines and adopts safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from teacher to student. A broad family of distillation techniques has been developed—logit (soft-label) matching, feature and layer-wise mimicry, multi-teacher and confidence-weighted schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—enabling deployment across vision, language, graphs, recommender systems, and federated settings. While distillation often preserves most teacher performance and can even improve student generalization, effectiveness depends on what is transferred, layer alignment, teacher quality, availability and match of data, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the operational variants, key empirical findings, domain-specific applications, common failure modes, and practical recommendations distilled from the provided studies.

papers_seen.author: Oconnor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Foundational, Task‑Aware, and Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD reduces memory and latency and can preserve much of a teacher’s performance when deployed thoughtfully. However, its reliability depends on careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to select or synthesize data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques and safeguards against bias and distributional failure. I argue KD should be treated as the practical core of an integrated, task-aware compression toolkit rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — An Argument for Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely adopted approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Empirical evidence across modalities shows KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of transferred signals, and availability or synthesis of appropriate data. For robust, fair, and production-ready compression, KD should operate as a configurable core within integrated pipelines that combine representation matching, data strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer adaptation).

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or synthesized examples—and can be organized in diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, and data‑free regimes). When combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. However, KD’s success is strongly context dependent: it depends on teacher quality and calibration, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and match of distillation data (or quality of synthetic surrogates), and careful objective and pipeline design to avoid propagating teacher errors or degrading long‑tail behaviour. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline, not a universal panacea.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Component for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD supports multiple transfer targets and training protocols, interoperates with complementary compression techniques, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and distribution shift determine outcomes, so KD should be applied as a task- and deployment-aware component within integrated compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool: Integrating Distillation with Representation, Data, and Architecture Strategies for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, more deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient to meet real-world deployment constraints: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention), and access to or synthesis of suitable training data. Best results arise when KD is embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level matching, projector or layer-mapping modules, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Careful attention to optimization, robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors is required to avoid propagating teacher errors and to produce reliable compact models for downstream applications.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component: The Case for Integrated, Task‑Aware Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applied method for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students. KD variants (logits, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols) have enabled practical deployment across vision, language, retrieval, generative modeling, and healthcare. However, KD faces concrete limitations—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena, and potential fairness or robustness regressions—that reduce its effectiveness when used alone. The strongest practical outcomes come from integrating KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful selection or synthesis of distilled supervision, and task- and data-aware training schedules.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive signals) and across diverse protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data-free/privacy-aware schemes). When combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely enables large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Its empirical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Hurley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal signals from larger teacher models into smaller, resource-efficient student models. The field encompasses simple logits-based soft-target transfer as well as richer objectives that match intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and uses protocols that include offline, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—and when distillation signals, layer alignment, and training data are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks) but faces reproducible failure modes (capacity and optimization mismatch, distribution shift, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and propagation of teacher biases or privacy risks) that motivate targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line Tool within Integrated Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across modalities. KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when configured to transfer appropriate signals (logits, features, attention, relations) and combined with complementary compression primitives. However, KD is context dependent: teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of bias and rare‑case degradation matter. I argue KD should serve as the default first‑line compression mechanism, but always as a configurable component of an integrated pipeline that explicitly addresses data regimes, architecture co‑design, and fairness/robustness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad toolbox for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models to smaller, faster, or privacy-preserving models. Methods range from soft-logit supervision to internal representation matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence across vision, NLP, graphs, and federated settings shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance in resource-constrained deployments, while challenges remain in teacher selection, data availability, bias propagation, and task-specific design.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Practical Model Compression: Evidence, Techniques, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable paradigm for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative models) and use-cases (edge deployment, federated learning, domain adaptation, continual learning), distillation has repeatedly enabled dramatic reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining or even improving task performance. However, distillation is not a panacea: careful design of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student inputs and layers, and when to apply supplementary strategies (adversarial examples, multi-teacher weighting, continual updates) is necessary to avoid failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, misalignment across detectors, and limits in compressing some model families. Drawing on empirical results and method innovations across the literature, I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational component of any deployment-oriented model compression pipeline, and that combining complementary distillation techniques tailored to the task and architecture yields the best balance of compactness, speed, and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically proven family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD supports a broad set of transfer signals and protocols and routinely improves deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy) when integrated with complementary compression methods. Its success is conditional on choices about teacher selection, student capacity and architecture, distilled signals, data regime, and explicit mitigation of teacher errors, rare-output degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Wallace

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A rich family of distillation targets and protocols has been developed (from soft logits to feature- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants), and KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware data and architecture strategies. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and augmentation, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Practical Model-Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for converting large teacher models into compact, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression primitives and with intentional choices about what and how to transfer. At the same time, KD is not automatic: reliable deployment requires addressing teacher–student mismatch, data limitations, and the risk of propagating undesirable behaviors. I argue that KD should be adopted as a central, context‑sensitive component of hybrid compression pipelines whose design is driven by task constraints and by explicit mitigation strategies for known failure modes.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a variety of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure, and contrastive objectives), training protocols (offline, online/co-distillation, multi‑teacher, and self‑distillation), and data strategies (real-data, synthetic or generator-based, data‑free, and federated) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely achieves favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities when its design is matched to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context‑sensitive: its reliability depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, mitigation of transferred errors and biases, and integration with complementary compression and data practices. Open challenges remain in principled transfer design, robust data‑free and privacy‑aware distillation, heterogeneous teacher–student alignment, and automating end‑to‑end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across modalities and tasks, distillation is used to transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from larger, more accurate teachers to smaller, faster students; it also appears within automated model search, pruning and distributed training workflows. Work in this area spans logit matching, representation-level objectives, data-free and few-shot regimes, multi-/online-teacher schemes, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling large reductions in memory and compute, but limitations remain around optimization, data availability, and the preservation or mitigation of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring predictive behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. KD spans logits-based supervision, feature and relational matching, adversarial or synthetic data generation, and architectural or curriculum adaptations. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD can enable deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings and sometimes yield students that match or exceed teacher performance, but it also carries risks—propagating teacher errors and biases, struggling under data scarcity or mismatch, and requiring task-specific engineering. I argue KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines, applied conditionally with targeted remedies and validated against task and deployment constraints.

Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD is most effective when treated as a central element of a broader compression portfolio that includes architecture-aware design, pre-training, pruning/quantization, and privacy- or data-aware protocols. Practical deployment benefits from careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align teacher and student, and when to apply auxiliary methods; remaining challenges include robustness under distributional shift, teacher imperfections, low-frequency token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a broadly applicable and practical paradigm for compressing large neural models, transferring functionality across architectures, enabling deployment under data- or communication-constraints, and improving interpretability and task adaptation. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants (layer mapping, feature matching, data-free generation, progressive replacement, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, and task-adaptive architecture search) provide complementary solutions to real-world constraints such as limited compute, limited data, privacy, and distribution shift. The most effective KD strategies select or synthesize the right supervision (soft targets, intermediate features, or distilled data), adapt the teacher–student alignment mechanism to the task, and account for practical issues such as imperfect teachers or label-smoothing interactions.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models. Across vision and language tasks KD has enabled substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving most teacher performance. Practical deployments use KD as one component in an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—and require task‑aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degraded performance on long‑tail or rare outputs, and sensitivity to distribution shift; these motivate multi‑teacher, selective, or data‑synthesis protocols and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Settings, and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies are now widespread across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and specialized settings (federated, few-shot, multi-modal, generative). Research has advanced along multiple axes: what to transfer (logits, features, attention, latent modules), how to shape the transfer (sample selection, adversarially-informed examples, curriculum, teacher ensembles, meta-learning), and special protocols for constrained environments (federated/black-box, few-shot, on-device inference). Empirical work shows KD can substantially close the performance gap between small and large models, enable practical deployment of generative and discriminative models, and, when extended, transfer robustness and interpretability. Remaining challenges include error propagation from teachers (especially for low-frequency phenomena), limitations under data heterogeneity in federated settings, and task-specific design choices for complex outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, set outputs), motivating continued work on tailored distillation objectives and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Configurable, but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful paradigm for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller, deployable students. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving much of teacher performance, and its toolkit spans logits, intermediate features, attention and relational objectives, data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher schemes. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to source or synthesize data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. When treated as the configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline and validated against distribution shift, capacity limits, and ethical concerns, KD delivers the best tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Spencer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Component for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, more deployable students. When treated as a configurable part of an integrated compression pipeline and tailored to task, data, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields strong trade-offs between efficiency and task performance. However, KD has concrete limits—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher artifacts or biases, and difficulty preserving low-frequency phenomena—that necessitate complementary methods and careful engineering. This review argues that KD should be regarded as essential but not sufficient on its own, and outlines practical recommendations and open directions for robust, context-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When adapted to task, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of a teacher's performance while enabling lower latency, smaller memory footprint, and improved adaptability across domains and modalities. However, KD is a family of techniques rather than a single algorithm: best outcomes arise from combining distillation with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, architecture search, curriculum design, data synthesis) and from explicitly addressing challenges such as imperfect teachers, domain shift, privacy, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible set of techniques to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, generative modeling, and structured prediction domains, KD variants — including logit transfer, feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations — provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, low-precision numerics, pruning and layer skipping, or teacher training tailored to students, distillation yields practical, deployable models applicable to constrained hardware and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Lara
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Core for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a practical engineering tool, KD reliably reduces inference cost, memory use, and latency across modalities while often preserving most of a teacher's performance. However, KD is not a universal or standalone solution: its effectiveness is conditional on teacher and student design, data regimes, choice of distilled signals, and careful integration with complementary compression primitives and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Treated as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline, KD offers the best balance between efficiency and fidelity for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD provides multiple transfer signals and training protocols that, when combined with complementary compression techniques, enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness is highly context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and objective design shape outcomes and failure modes. Practical use emphasizes configurable pipelines that integrate distillation with data strategies and other compression primitives while addressing robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational objectives) and through multiple protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical and practical work shows that KD, when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with task‑aware data and curriculum strategies, often preserves much of teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost; however, its effectiveness is strongly context‑dependent and requires deliberate mitigation of failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare‑token behavior, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Essential, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used as Part of an Integrated Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical and methodological work across vision, language, graph, and recommendation systems shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, latency, and memory. However, KD’s success is strongly context-dependent: it requires task-aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and deployment constraints. Responsible, robust compression therefore treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses complementary techniques and explicit mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, speech, detection, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher protocols—enable substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, data strategy, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression (e.g., pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical deployments use task-aware adaptations, confidence- or curriculum-based weighting, and privacy- or federated-aware designs; remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, distribution shift, rare-output transfer, and principled theory for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of methods for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD techniques operate at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures—and in varied protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware data and optimization strategies, KD routinely produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Nevertheless, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and selection of data, and protocol design. Key open problems include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under distribution shift and heterogeneous architectures, preservation of low‑frequency/long‑tail behaviors, and privacy/fairness‑aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The literature provides a diverse toolbox—logit/soft-target matching, feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or adversarial synthesis—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirically, KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks when care is taken to align teacher and student, choose appropriate distillation targets, and adapt to the available data regime. Remaining practical and scientific challenges include teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity and privacy, robustness and distribution shift, propagation of teacher biases, and reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gonzales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Dependent Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable and practical family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers, routinely recovering much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and objective design, and it must be integrated with complementary compression techniques and safeguards to mitigate risks such as teacher errors, bias transfer, and degraded low‑frequency behavior. When treated as a configurable core of a compression pipeline and validated against deployment constraints, KD typically yields the best accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable core of broader compression pipelines, guided by task-aware design, teacher–student co‑engineering, and targeted mitigations for bias, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. It supports multiple information-transfer mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and can be adapted to constrained settings (limited data, privacy, heterogeneous devices). KD is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or pretraining—and when practitioners mitigate known failure modes such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, or teacher–student mismatch. With careful design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, which data to use), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while largely preserving task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated, practical family of methods for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD often preserves most teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but it can also transfer teacher biases or degrade rare-token behavior; therefore it should be treated as a configurable, task-aware component of end-to-end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance

papers_seen.author: Sampson

papers_seen.author: Potter

papers_seen.author: Burton

papers_seen.author: Mccall

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across domains and tasks—language modeling and translation, recommendation, graph learning, vision, continual and domain adaptation, and resource-constrained deployment—KD enables trade-offs between accuracy, latency, memory, privacy, and train-time complexity. Variants such as feature mimicking, self- and teacher-free distillation, ensemble and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations extend KD’s applicability. At the same time, careful choice of training targets, treatment of low-frequency phenomena, and consideration of the teacher-student mismatch are necessary to avoid transferring teacher errors and to realize the full benefits of distillation.

papers_seen.author: Marks
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A wide set of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive structure), training paradigms (offline, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation), and data strategies (real, synthetic, or data‑free) have been developed. KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count, but reliable success depends on deliberate, task‑aware choices about transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of bias, robustness, and distributional risks.

papers_seen.author: Rodgers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, accurate teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching into a diverse toolkit (feature/attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and data-free protocols) that is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but its effectiveness is highly context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of bias and distributional mismatch strongly influence outcomes. Practical use treats KD as a configurable core component of integrated compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students. KD provides a rich toolkit—soft‑target/logit matching, intermediate‑feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation, and data‑free or synthetic‑data methods—and frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime, choice of distilled signals and losses, and careful integration with complementary compression primitives. For robust, real‑world deployment KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline, combined with targeted design, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer behavior and/or internal structure from larger, often ensemble or multi-modal teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels—from soft-label supervision to intermediate-feature, attention, and relational matching—and are widely used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under memory or latency constraints, and support domain or modality adaptation. The effectiveness of KD depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and careful design of what and how knowledge is transferred; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and targeted training protocols improves reliability in practice.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression encompass a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or richer models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models. Across computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, graph learning, federated settings, and multi-modal systems, KD variants—ranging from feature- and layer-wise matching to self-distillation, data-free adversarial schemes, and task-aware filtering—have been applied to address capacity gaps, domain shifts, privacy constraints, and inference latency. Empirical and methodological work shows that careful alignment between teacher and student (in representation, task relevance, or sample selection), consideration of data heterogeneity, and incorporation of pre-training or auxiliary objectives improve student performance. Open challenges include robust distillation under heterogeneous architectures and non-iid data, mitigating bias transfer, and designing distillation objectives that prioritize downstream task relevance while remaining communication- and privacy-efficient.

Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and mitigation of transferred biases and robustness deficits.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers.
