papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Modalities, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high-performing deep learning models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. A broad set of distillation strategies—ranging from soft-label supervision and feature mimicking to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, adversarially guided feature transfer, self-distillation, and automated architecture search guided by teacher models—enable substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while preserving or even improving performance across vision, language, multimodal, and sequence tasks. Best practice combines input-side methods (data augmentation and mixup), representation-level transfer, and careful teacher-student design choices to match the deployment objectives (efficiency, fairness, interpretability, or privacy).

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer behavior or internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to reduce latency, memory, and communication costs while retaining performance. Across modalities, researchers have developed logits-based supervision, feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and architecture-aware compression. These methods are applied to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, federated and privacy-sensitive settings, domain adaptation, generative-model compression, and improved fairness or robustness when combined with task-aware design. Despite strong empirical gains, important challenges remain in handling distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous architectures, and data-scarce or data-free scenarios. Emerging directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, joint optimization with pruning and NAS, federated/distilled learning across heterogeneous devices, and cross-modal distillation for generative and segmentation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide flexible, broadly applicable ways to transfer performance from large teacher models to compact student models so they can run under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, relational signals) and procedures (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis) have been developed and integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, ensembling). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and recommendation systems shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve deployability, though success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases. Remaining directions include automated, task-adaptive transfer choices, robust data-free distillation, and principled controls for fairness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Foundational, Context-Dependent Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a flexible framework for producing compact, deployable models and for transferring behavior across domains, modalities, and privacy-constrained settings. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD enables significant reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, distillation has clear failure modes (optimization gaps, distributional mismatch, and social harms) that require targeted mitigation and careful evaluation. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, application-driven toolkit for model compression and adaptation, not a one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core technique for producing compact, efficient models and for enabling cross-model, cross-modal, and privacy-sensitive transfer in deep learning and NLP. KD can be implemented at the logit, feature, and layer levels, and extended to ensemble teachers, data-free scenarios, federated settings, and task-adaptive architecture search. While KD often yields large efficiency gains with small accuracy loss, its effectiveness depends on data properties, teacher–student alignment, and training choices; addressing limitations such as data heterogeneity, low-frequency token degradation, and mismatched inputs requires tailored methods (e.g., feature mimicking, teacher adaptation, multi-teacher weighting, and specialized divergences). Building on empirical and methodological work across modalities, I argue that KD should be treated as a versatile, application-driven toolkit rather than a single recipe, and that future progress will come from combining representational-level distillation, teacher-aware training, and methods that reduce reliance on original training data.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. Across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and recommender systems, KD methods have been developed to match outputs (soft targets), internal representations (features and attention), relational or contrastive signals, and task-specific rank or ordering information. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability (including data-free strategies), and integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Trade-offs include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena, and optimization challenges; many works propose curricula, student-friendly teacher training, or multi-teacher and online protocols to mitigate these issues. The field has matured into a central engineering primitive for deployment, while continuing to pursue principled transfer objectives, privacy-aware distillation, and robust domain- and architecture-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across vision and NLP. KD works at multiple levels (logits, features, layers) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. At the same time, KD has concrete limitations (teacher imperfections, data scarcity, student capacity mismatch) that require deliberate mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation Is Essential but Context‑Sensitive for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely adopted toolkit for producing compact models that approach the performance of larger teachers. KD routinely delivers favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities when it is chosen and configured with attention to what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and the available data regime. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded long‑tail/low‑frequency behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques that make large, high-performing models practical for deployment by transferring behavior, representations, or decision structure to smaller models. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when combined with appropriate supervision signals, data practices, and architectural alignment, but it also has important failure modes—propagated teacher errors, sensitivity to data distribution and teacher quality, and limits when student capacity is insufficient. I argue KD should be treated as a foundational component of model-compression pipelines, applied thoughtfully and in combination with complementary methods (augmentation, pruning/quantization, privacy mechanisms, and federated protocols) to realize robust, efficient systems for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models by transferring information from larger or specialized models. It supports a broad range of objectives beyond raw compression—improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, supporting privacy-aware or federated workflows, and permitting deployment on constrained hardware. KD methods range from simple soft-label matching to richer transfers of intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive structure. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, alignment between teacher and student, data availability and distribution, and the choice of signals and losses. When applied with attention to these constraints and combined sensibly with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), KD is a practical foundational technique for real-world model compression in vision, language, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Ingram
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Integrated Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD reliably delivers large efficiency gains across vision, speech, and NLP when its objectives, data strategy, and teacher–student design are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its best outcomes arise when it is treated as a configurable, context‑aware core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and rare‑event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical framework for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving functionality across modalities. When combined with task-aware choices of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods, KD enables large reductions in model size and latency with modest performance loss and can also address privacy, robustness, and deployment constraints. However, KD has failure modes — including propagation of teacher biases, difficulty with low-frequency phenomena, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional shifts — that require targeted remedies. Careful design, including multi-signal objectives, teacher scheduling, exposure to raw or synthesized data, and joint optimization with pruning or architecture search, makes KD an indispensable component of practical model-deployment toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints and supports cross-modal and domain transfer. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and complementary compression and training practices. Reliable compression treats distillation as a core component of a broader, task-aware pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task‑aware distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, realizing robust, fair, and reliable compressed models requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, the nature and availability of distillation data, and targeted remedies for known failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving functionality. Beyond simple size reduction, distillation enables device deployment, privacy-preserving releases, latency reduction, ensemble compression, improved low-precision accuracy, and better generalization when combined with complementary techniques. Successful deployment requires matching distillation method to problem structure (e.g., graphs, vision-language, transformers), addressing teacher-induced biases, and adopting strategies such as data-free synthesis, task-aware layer selection, relational objectives, and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Ubiquitous, but Demand-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing high-capacity models into efficient students across modalities and tasks. Empirical results across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and generative settings show KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, features, attention, contrastive objectives), the alignment between teacher and student inputs, the data used for distillation, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Carefully chosen distillation algorithms and extensions (self-supervised distillation, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, online and distributed schemes, and privacy-preserving perturbations) can mitigate common failure modes and broaden KD’s applicability in production and research settings.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. The literature shows a diverse set of objectives and protocols—soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, many-to-many layer mappings, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and adversarial or generator-based sample augmentation—that together enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while trading off accuracy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical results indicate distilled students often approach teacher performance with substantially lower cost, but important limitations persist (teacher bias transfer, low-frequency token degradation, data access constraints, and capacity mismatch), motivating hybrid pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and versatile toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. A broad family of distillation objectives and protocols has been developed—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational, contrastive, adversarial, and data‑free approaches—and KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit handling of distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. The literature converges on a diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, decision-boundary samples), training protocols (single/multi-teacher, teacher-annealing, self- or online-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data approaches), and architecture-aware adaptations (many-to-many layer mapping, projector adapters, and combinations with pruning/quantization). Empirical studies across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and generative tasks show distilled students can recover much teacher performance and sometimes yield superior efficiency–accuracy trade-offs; nonetheless, open problems remain around data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, preserving low-frequency behaviors, and transferring robustness and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD has been adapted across logits-, feature-, and relation-level objectives, combined with complementary compression primitives, and applied in specialized settings (federated, data-free, recommender, and generative). Its practical value is substantial, but realizing that value requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Morrow
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD supports a range of transfer signals and training protocols and routinely reduces latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance in many settings. However, KD is context dependent: its success hinges on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and mitigation of failure modes. As a result, KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone, sufficient solution.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The literature frames KD as a flexible, task-aware toolbox: common transfer targets include softened logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and contrastive or adversarial objectives; training regimes span offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free protocols; and KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-augmentation or synthesis. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while producing substantial efficiency gains (reduced FLOPs, memory, and latency), but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of signals to transfer, and the availability or generation of appropriate data. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable core component of integrated compression pipelines and emphasize safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data schemes, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and objective design. Important open problems include principled theory linking transfer signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under domain shift and heterogeneous devices, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Conditional, and Best Integrated into Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile set of techniques for transferring behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities, but its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and careful mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Therefore KD should be treated as a configurable core component of integrated compression workflows—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—rather than a turnkey, standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Conley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Tool for Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and internal structure from larger teachers into smaller students. Across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, KD yields substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression primitives. KD is therefore best treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical and flexible pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across NLP and other modalities, researchers have developed logit-level, representation-level, layer-wise, multi-teacher, data-free, privacy-aware, and task-aware distillation variants and combined KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows that careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and low-frequency phenomena materially affects student quality and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Coffey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods span soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or contrastive objectives, and specialized protocols for data-free, federated, cross‑modal, and adversarial settings. KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Settings, and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies are now widespread across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and specialized settings (federated, few-shot, multi-modal, generative). Research has advanced along multiple axes: what to transfer (logits, features, attention, latent modules), how to shape the transfer (sample selection, adversarially-informed examples, curriculum, teacher ensembles, meta-learning), and special protocols for constrained environments (federated/black-box, few-shot, on-device inference). Empirical work shows KD can substantially close the performance gap between small and large models, enable practical deployment of generative and discriminative models, and, when extended, transfer robustness and interpretability. Remaining challenges include error propagation from teachers (especially for low-frequency phenomena), limitations under data heterogeneity in federated settings, and task-specific design choices for complex outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, set outputs), motivating continued work on tailored distillation objectives and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically proven family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD supports a broad set of transfer signals and protocols and routinely improves deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy) when integrated with complementary compression methods. Its success is conditional on choices about teacher selection, student capacity and architecture, distilled signals, data regime, and explicit mitigation of teacher errors, rare-output degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior and performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when integrated thoughtfully into compression pipelines and paired with complementary techniques, but its effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student design, data strategy, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes what the provided literature collectively reports about knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques: commonly used distillation objectives and training protocols, empirical patterns of when and how KD helps across modalities, practical constraints and failure modes (data availability, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency/structured outputs, privacy and bias transfer), and targeted solutions (data-free/zero-shot distillation, teacher engineering, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and combinations with pruning/quantization and architecture search). The goal is to give a concise map of methods, observed trade-offs, and open problems for researchers and practitioners working on compressing or adapting large models for resource- or deployment-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, heterogeneous hardware). Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft‑label/logit matching to intermediate feature, attention, relational, adversarial, and data‑free schemes—routinely improve student performance and often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy when designed with task‑ and capacity‑aware choices. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of integrated compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, and architecture search and when practitioners explicitly address data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and robustness or fairness safeguards. Important open problems remain around distribution shift, low‑frequency behavior, privacy‑sensitive distillation, heterogeneous architectures, and principled theory for different transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Bryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical, Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. When designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, distilled signals, and data regime, distillation routinely yields compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, energy, and privacy constraints. However, distillation is context dependent: it must be integrated with complementary compression methods and targeted mitigations for teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, distribution shift, and low‑frequency behaviors in order to produce reliable, production‑ready models.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained devices, and support privacy- or resource-constrained settings. Approaches span soft-label distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, data-free and zero-shot methods, multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, self-distillation, task- and modality-specific objectives, and combinations with pruning. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D detection, recommender systems, and multiple NLP tasks demonstrates that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while significantly reducing latency and memory. The literature also provides growing theoretical insight into when and how distillation helps, and identifies open challenges including imperfect teachers, domain shift, low-frequency token fidelity, modality mismatch, and heterogeneous-device federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD methods encompass soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and data‑free protocols, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD frequently recovers a large portion of teacher performance and enables deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints, its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and data regime. For robust, high-fidelity compression, KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline that includes safeguards and complementary techniques to address known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Berry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior or internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Empirically, KD reduces inference latency, memory footprint, and compute while often preserving most of a teacher's task performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how data are used (real, augmented, synthesized, or zero-shot), and whether distillation is performed online, with multiple teachers, or self-supervised. KD is most effective when configured to task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search). It also has well-documented failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagated teacher artifacts, degraded long-tail performance, and data-availability or privacy limits—that require explicit mitigation strategies. This synthesis summarizes established techniques, practical trade-offs, and actionable design patterns for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Goodman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods include output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self- and multi-teacher protocols, and data‑free or privacy-aware synthesis. When combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely produces substantial reductions in latency, memory, and parameter footprint while retaining much of teacher performance. The effectiveness of KD is highly context dependent: it relies on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis strategies, and explicit treatment of robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include principled teacher–student design, reliable distillation under data scarcity and distribution shift, mitigation of bias transfer, and automation of distillation pipelines.

For robust, production‑grade compression KD should be treated as the central building block of an integrated, task‑aware pipeline that combines representational distillation, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), while explicitly mitigating bias transfer, low‑frequency degradation, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.title: The Centrality and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. Beyond reducing parameter counts and inference latency, distillation enables transferring inductive biases, protecting privacy in federated settings, enabling few- and zero-shot compression, and supporting task-adaptive and automated compression workflows. However, distillation is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity, teacher–student mismatch, and redundant teacher representations can limit gains. Best practice combines representation-level and layer-aware techniques, multi-teacher or teacher-free strategies where appropriate, and task-aware selection of distilled information to maximize compressed-model utility.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component: The Case for Integrated, Task‑Aware Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applied method for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students. KD variants (logits, feature- and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols) have enabled practical deployment across vision, language, retrieval, generative modeling, and healthcare. However, KD faces concrete limitations—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena, and potential fairness or robustness regressions—that reduce its effectiveness when used alone. The strongest practical outcomes come from integrating KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful selection or synthesis of distilled supervision, and task- and data-aware training schedules.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression That Must Be Task‑Aware and Integrated
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core technique that is combined with task-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and that explicitly mitigates risks such as bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade KD variants—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to representation-level matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols—have been adapted to many tasks and modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal, generative models, and federated settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves most teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and optimization. Remaining challenges include principled theory for when and what to transfer, reliable distillation across heterogeneous architectures and non‑i.i.d. data, mitigation of bias and teacher errors, and robust data-free or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ortega
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for producing compact models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. It offers multiple mechanisms (soft-targets, intermediate representation matching, attention- or channel-wise transfers, multi-teacher and data‑free variants) that, when combined with complementary compression techniques, can yield substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, KD’s effectiveness is highly dependent on task, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints; consequently, it should be treated as an adaptable component within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: State of the Art, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated set of techniques for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. KD variants and complementary compression methods enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous hardware across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and generative tasks. Success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teachers and students, how to handle limited or private data, and how to integrate distillation with pretraining and other compression methods. Remaining challenges include teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, preserving low-frequency behaviors, and robust data-free or federated distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across modalities and tasks, a broad set of distillation targets and protocols—ranging from soft logits to intermediate feature and attention matching, relational or contrastive signals, and data‑free synthesis—has enabled substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance. Effectiveness is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and careful design of objectives, layer alignment, and complementary compression steps determine outcomes. Open problems include principled theory of transfer, robust transfer under distribution shift or privacy constraints, and preserving rare or structured outputs in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Methods include matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online protocols, and data‑aware or data‑free variants. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable tool within an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias propagation, rare‑token degradation, and distribution shift. Practical deployments therefore combine careful selection of transfer targets, layer and projector design, curricula and data synthesis, and complementary compression primitives while monitoring robustness, fairness, and privacy.
