papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Hayden
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded framework for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary teacher models into compact students. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, data-free or zero-shot schemes, and self-distillation. Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance when combined with suitable data strategies, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD’s effectiveness is context dependent: success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and safeguards against transferred artifacts, distributional mismatch, and social harms. The practical consensus treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — Advocating Integrated Compression Pipelines for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, empirically validated approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models, enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. While KD reliably recovers much of teacher performance across modalities when carefully designed, it is context-sensitive: its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Consequently, KD should be treated as the core component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware distillation signals, architecture-aware adaptations, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Central but Context‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practically effective set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, distillation yields substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often recovering much of teacher performance. However, its success is highly context dependent: outcomes hinge on teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals and training protocol, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. For robust, fair, and production-ready compression, distillation should be deployed as a configurable core within integrated pipelines that combine architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, privacy, and long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while often preserving much of the original performance. A broad toolkit has been developed—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and channel-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—that is applied across vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, and generative modeling. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is effective in many settings but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful objective and alignment choices; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of a larger compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Stanley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. KD spans matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free protocols, and multi- or online-teacher schemes. Empirical work shows KD typically recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can interact positively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and explicit mitigation of bias, distribution shift, and low-frequency failures. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and deployment-ready students while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation techniques include matching logits (soft labels), feature- and layer-level imitation, ensemble and online schemes, data-free approaches, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on teacher quality and design, how and what information is transferred, availability and nature of data used for distillation, and how distillation is integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications span NLP (BERT compression, reading comprehension, language generation), vision and generative models (GANs, lipreading, 3D detection), recommender systems, and graphs. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher-student architectures, preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, preventing transfer of teacher biases, and robust distillation under distribution shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Rose
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. KD encompasses many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free and privacy-aware variants). Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines appropriate distillation objectives with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies) and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach to compress large or ensemble models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, distillation can recover accuracy for lightweight architectures, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and transfer specialized properties (e.g., temporal, structural, or ensemble knowledge). However, distillation is not a panacea: its success depends on the choice of teacher, student architecture and capacity, the training protocol (including data augmentation and sample selection), and implementation details that affect optimization. When these factors are treated carefully, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, architecture design, quantization) and can be adapted to domain-specific needs such as federated learning, retrieval, and vision-language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Sensitive Path for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven and versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around appropriate transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, and data regimes, KD frequently enables substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on task and deployment constraints, and KD must often be combined with complementary methods and task-aware design to avoid failure modes and to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Cross-Domain Argument for Practical, Responsible, and Multi-Modal Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative domains, distillation methods can preserve most of a teacher's performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication. Best results come from (a) matching appropriate internal representations (layer mapping, attention, many-to-many mappings), (b) designing teachers or multi-teacher schemes that are student-aware, and (c) combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, NAS, adversarial training, federated schemes). However, practitioners must be mindful of failure modes—bias amplification, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, and gaps when no training data are available—and adopt targeted mitigations such as task-adaptive compression, confidence-aware multi-teacher weighting, and data-free or privacy-preserving distillation when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context‑Dependent for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides a flexible set of transfer signals and training protocols that enable substantial efficiency gains when paired with appropriate data strategies and complementary compression primitives. However, KD is context‑dependent: its effectiveness hinges on teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted safeguards against bias and distributional mismatch, so it should be applied as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile toolkit for producing compact models from larger teachers. When designed and validated against task and deployment constraints, KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute; however, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and complementary compression and safeguarding measures.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable, and Context‑Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, fast, and deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely yields meaningful efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks when it is treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline. However, its practical success is conditional on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Responsible deployment therefore combines KD with complementary compression methods and monitoring suited to the task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of risks such as bias transfer and distribution-shift degradation.

papers_seen.author: Sawyer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. The literature converges on a taxonomy of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and engineering integrations (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation/search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can yield compact models suitable for constrained hardware or privacy-sensitive deployments. Success is highly context-dependent and hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation strategies for bias, distribution shift, and rare/low-frequency phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a single plug‑and‑play solution.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Methods vary by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), by how teachers and students are arranged (offline, online, ensemble, self-distillation), and by how distillation is integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free regimes). KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can improve robustness or generalization in some settings, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful handling of bias, distribution shift, and privacy considerations.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables deployment across modalities when integrated thoughtfully with complementary compression methods. Its success is context dependent — determined by teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and loss of rare behaviors — so practitioners should treat KD as a configurable element of a broader compression pipeline rather than a one-shot solution.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Not Panacea Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted technique for compressing large models into smaller ones and transferring capabilities across tasks and modalities. When thoughtfully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or augmenting data, and matching teacher-student capacity—KD yields substantial gains in inference efficiency with modest performance loss and can enable deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, optimization dynamics, and architecture alignment; complementary tools (pretraining, projector modules, online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols) and careful engineering are often required to realize consistent, robust results. Open directions include principled data-free distillation, better theoretical characterizations of what is transferred, and joint co-design of architectures and distillation objectives for specific deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Greene
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Practical, and Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, choice of distilled signals, and data availability. Best results arise when KD is treated as a configurable toolkit integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful layer- and task-alignment, and safeguards for bias, privacy, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool that Requires Task-Aware, Complementary Engineering
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for producing compact models from large teachers that supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints and student capacity. Best outcomes arise when KD is treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, data- and task-aware strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Dependent, Foundational Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller student models. KD encompasses many mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, data‑free and multi‑teacher schemes) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, curriculum, domain adaptation). Its power for deployment in resource‑ or privacy‑constrained settings is well documented; however, KD is not universally sufficient. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher‑student compatibility, data availability, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization mismatch, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. The pragmatic stance advocated here is to treat KD as a configurable component of a broader compression and deployment pipeline, tuned to task, data regime, and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Context‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD consistently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs when applied thoughtfully, but its benefits are conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and architecture alignment. Best practice treats KD as the central component of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and explicit mitigations for failure modes such as propagated bias, distribution shift, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate-feature matching, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-free or generator-driven protocols—routinely recover a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression primitives. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; consequently KD is most reliable when used as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, pretraining, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Acosta
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks. KD methods span matching soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals, and extend to online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free and privacy‑aware protocols. Empirical and methodological work shows KD often recovers a substantial fraction of teacher performance when combined with task‑aware choices and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), but its success is context‑sensitive: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Clay
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, broadly applicable mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models and is essential for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or hardware‑optimal deployment: it must be designed in a task‑aware way, combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and paired with data and curriculum strategies to mitigate failure modes such as teacher bias, poor low‑frequency behavior, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable core inside an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable production outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of risks such as bias transfer and distribution-shift degradation.

papers_seen.author: Klein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of methods that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or otherwise stronger teacher models into smaller, faster, or more constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic data, privacy-aware public data). Empirically, KD routinely yields large reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while preserving a substantial fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but its success is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, distillation targets, data availability and selection, and deployment constraints determine outcomes. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable core of model-compression workflows and emphasize safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy along with ongoing work on theory and low-data or cross-domain distillation.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high‑capacity teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, generative and multimodal tasks, KD has been adapted into many targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with architecture‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the empirical strengths of KD, the principal methods and protocols, common limitations, and practical design patterns that guide successful compression and deployment.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Demand-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically powerful and practically versatile approach for compressing large models and transferring behavior to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities by matching logits, intermediate features, attention, or relational structure and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Recent work extends KD to settings with no original data, privacy constraints, heterogeneous architectures, and specialized tasks (graphs, non‑autoregressive generation, lifelong learning). However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher–student design, data strategies, and task-aware objectives, and important open problems remain (capacity mismatch, teacher bias transfer, preserving low-frequency behaviors, principled layer mapping, and rigorous theoretical understanding).

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical framework for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline/online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free/federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) allows practitioners to recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance across modalities when teacher–student compatibility, data strategy, and optimization design are carefully managed. KD is most reliable when embedded in a task‑aware compression pipeline that attends to data availability, teacher quality, student capacity, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; persistent challenges include principled theory for diverse objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context‑Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of larger teachers' performance. KD should be treated as a first‑order component of compression pipelines, but it is not sufficient on its own: reliable deployment requires task‑aware objective selection, attention to teacher–student compatibility and data regimes, and combination with complementary compression and privacy techniques.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) and within diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free/zero‑shot approaches). Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and can sometimes improve student generalization when objectives, data, and teacher–student design are well matched; however, success is context dependent and sensitive to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and distribution shift, and risks of transferring teacher errors or bias. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines carefully chosen distillation signals, layer-mapping and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) while adopting targeted safeguards for low‑frequency behaviors, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied framework for compressing large models, improving generalization, and transferring capabilities across modalities and deployment constraints. Research spans teacher-student paradigms (including multi-teacher and self-distillation), data-free and zero-shot distillation, task-adaptive compression, and applications to specialized tasks (detection, retrieval, translation, multimodal learning, federated settings, and graph problems). Empirical work shows KD can yield large speed and size gains while retaining much of the teacher's performance, but also exposes important limitations tied to optimization, data used for distillation, and potential bias transfer. Recent methods address these limitations via curriculum scheduling, confidence- or reinforcement-based teacher weighting, task-adaptive architecture search, domain- and modality-aware losses, and efficient label-generation or student-focused training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a foundational technique for compressing large models into efficient, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is effective across modalities (graphs, vision, speech, and NLP), supports privacy- and communication-constrained settings, can work without original training data, and admits algorithmic and theoretical refinements that improve robustness, interpretability, and efficiency. Combining representation-level objectives, adversarial or data-free sample generation, and task-aware layer mapping yields practical recipes for real-world compression and adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline: practitioners should select appropriate transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), adapt objectives to student capacity and data regime, and combine distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies). While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities, it is not a universal cure—limitations such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and the risk of propagating biases require targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature shows a diverse toolkit of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, channel statistics, and contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online, self-, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and task-aware adaptations (layer mapping, projector modules, synthetic-data generation, and curriculum/annealing). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, multimodal tasks, and continual or federated settings demonstrates substantial efficiency gains but also highlights persistent challenges: teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatch, limited or unavailable training data, propagation of teacher biases or errors, distribution shift, and difficulties transferring rare or low-frequency behaviors. Practical success typically requires matching the distillation signal to task and student capacity and integrating KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving or sometimes improving task performance. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component and combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, layer mapping, or data synthesis), KD yields favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities and supports deployment under latency, privacy, and data-constraint requirements. However, realizing KD's benefits reliably requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, what signals are transferred, how layers are aligned, and which training data or augmentations are used.

papers_seen.author: Franklin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practical Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. When distillation is designed with attention to which signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data regimes (including data-free or privacy-aware workflows), and when it is integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search), students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Despite empirical successes, KD’s effectiveness is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD variants—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self-distillation, and data-free protocols—are widely applied across vision, language, speech, graphs and multimodal tasks. Practical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and complementary compression techniques; best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable set of techniques that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to task and data constraints, KD unlocks deployment on latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained platforms while supporting modalities from language to vision and multimodal systems. However, KD is not automatic: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, rare-token degradation) are required for responsible, robust outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression, Robustness, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more robust models. Beyond mere size reduction, contemporary KD techniques transfer internal representations, enable deployment under data- and privacy-constrained conditions, mitigate architectural and modality mismatches, and interact non-trivially with regularization practices. I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational toolchain in applied deep learning and NLP systems—one that must be combined with tailored alignment, privacy-preserving, and teacher-selection strategies to fully realize its benefits in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated, flexible family of methods for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teachers into smaller students. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs when the distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen to match the task and deployment constraints. However, KD is not an automatic solution: it requires representation-aware objectives, careful handling of data and capacity mismatch, and integration with complementary compression primitives and safeguards to avoid failure modes such as bias transfer, loss of rare behaviors, and domain-shift fragility. When treated as a configurable core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play fix, KD enables responsible, practical deployment of deep models across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Pragmatic, Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, distillation can preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployments with constrained compute, memory, latency, and privacy requirements. However, its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints (e.g., robustness, heterogeneity, data availability). When applied thoughtfully—using feature-based objectives, ensemble or adversarial strategies, data augmentation or data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression—KD reliably delivers practical trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Demand-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' utility. KD methods span output matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, self- and ensemble-distillation, meta-learned and student-friendly teacher designs, and data- or task-aware adaptations. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks demonstrates KD’s ability to deliver large reductions in model size and compute with modest performance loss, and in many cases to improve robustness or generalization when combined with appropriate procedures. At the same time, KD’s reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these constraints through architectural design, curriculum and meta-learning, augmentation and synthetic-data strategies, and multi-teacher or online schemes is central to practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher–student soft-label transfer into a flexible set of methods that enable compact, fast, and often more robust models across vision, language, multimodal and generative settings. When designed with awareness of task constraints, data availability, and deployment demands, KD combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, layer skipping, meta-learned teachers, or generative replay) reliably yields practical gains. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a first-class, configurable component in compression pipelines: powerful and broadly applicable when paired with principled, task-centered decisions, but demand-aware and tuned to deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Summers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while retaining much of task performance. Modern KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis. KD is commonly combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence indicates KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and suitable data strategies are aligned, but its success is context-dependent and requires task-aware design to mitigate limits related to teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Component for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective method for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD reduces inference cost and can preserve much of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data used for transfer, and optimization choices. KD is therefore best treated as a first‑class, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—paired with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and privacy-aware procedures—rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Miranda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When applied with task-aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary compression methods to employ, KD reliably yields large efficiency gains with modest loss in performance. However, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and explicit handling of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded rare-case behavior, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD not as a turnkey solution but as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal domains, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance; it is most effective when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation, and hardware-aware design). The literature also highlights several persistent challenges — teacher and capacity mismatch, optimization and data limitations, privacy and distribution shift — and converges on practical strategies such as careful choice of distillation signals, layer alignment, multi-teacher or online protocols, and synthetic-data or data-free approaches to operate under constrained access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are now core tools for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. The literature has expanded far beyond simple logits matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates broad applicability across modalities (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and generative models) and deployment contexts (edge devices, federated systems, and data-constrained settings). The main practical challenges are (1) choosing what and how to distill for a given task and student architecture, (2) coping with limited or unavailable original training data, (3) avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses (e.g., biases or low-frequency degradation), and (4) co-designing distillation with other compression primitives and hardware constraints. Progress comes from combining representational objectives, layer-mapping strategies, task-aware teacher selection, and safeguards (privacy or fairness) appropriate to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Context‑Aware, and Best Deployed in Hybrid Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure across vision and language tasks, but it is not a universal cure: its value depends on choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data, privacy, and bias concerns are handled. I argue KD should be a first‑line, configurable component of compression pipelines, augmented by teacher‑aware design, complementary compression primitives, and principled mitigations for its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, and privacy. The literature develops a broad taxonomy of distillation signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational maps, contrastive objectives), training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, self-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and federated), and integrations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while greatly improving efficiency, but success is context-dependent, hinging on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of bias, robustness, and privacy risks. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component within integrated compression pipelines rather than a standalone recipe, and open problems remain in principled choice of distilled targets, reliable distillation with limited or private data, and theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students. KD provides a rich toolkit—soft‑target/logit matching, intermediate‑feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation, and data‑free or synthetic‑data methods—and frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime, choice of distilled signals and losses, and careful integration with complementary compression primitives. For robust, real‑world deployment KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline, combined with targeted design, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy.
