papers_seen.author: Gallegos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Empirical evidence across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows KD routinely recovers much of the teacher’s performance and enables practical deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a drop‑in solution: its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and explicit measures to mitigate failure modes such as bias transfer, optimization gaps, and degraded handling of low‑frequency phenomena. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware core within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies, and robustness/fairness safeguards—yields the most reliable path to deployable, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate-feature matching, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-free or generator-driven protocols—routinely recover a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression primitives. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; consequently KD is most reliable when used as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, pretraining, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from large, often multi-modal or ensemble teachers into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD has been adapted into many forms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and offline protocols, and data-free or zero-shot schemes — and is frequently combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance in many settings when teacher quality, student capacity, and appropriate data or synthesis strategies are addressed; theoretical and empirical analyses highlight KD’s role both as knowledge transfer and as a regularizer. Despite broad success, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or heterogeneous data, and propagation of teacher artifacts; current best practice is to treat KD as one element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Mckinney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Task‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for producing compact models from larger teachers to meet latency, memory, energy, and privacy constraints. KD methods span outputs-level supervision, intermediate-representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data‑free synthesis, and multi- or self-distillation protocols. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with careful design about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. Nevertheless, KD is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis ability, and explicit mitigations for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines rather than a one-shot solution.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD operates through multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, synthetic data) and adapts across modalities (vision, speech, graphs, NLP) and deployment constraints (edge inference, federated settings, privacy-aware releases). While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its success depends on careful choices—teacher quality, what to match, layer alignment, projector usage, data selection, and privacy constraints—and benefits from combining complementary methods such as ensembling, task-adaptive architecture search, and federated or privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. When applied thoughtfully it can preserve most of a teacher model’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute; when combined with complementary compression primitives and task-aware design it enables robust, production-ready deployments. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases and rare-case failures. Best results arise from integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline with methods tailored to the target task and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond simple soft-logit matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and hybrids with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on careful alignment of objectives, teacher/student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and distributional failures. This review synthesizes methods, empirical patterns, limitations, and practical recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient models while preserving performance. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, researchers have applied KD for inference speedup, deployment on resource-constrained devices, privacy-preserving model release, and enhanced robustness or interpretability. Methods vary from standard teacher–student soft-label supervision to data-free distillation, adversarially chosen boundary samples, many-to-many layer mappings, generative replay, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss when combined with task-aware design, careful sample selection, and appropriate optimization; challenges remain around distributional mismatch, low-frequency token handling, heterogeneous architectures, and privacy/validation in data-free scenarios. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compressed models, joint optimization of pruning and KD, federated/distilled learning across heterogeneous devices, and cross-modal distillation for generative capabilities.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple logit-matching to a broad set of objectives and pipelines — including feature- and representation-matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial procedures, data-free and privacy-aware methods, multi-teacher schemes, teacher design, and selective sample strategies. KD has been applied across domains (NLP, vision, graph learning, generative models, novel-view synthesis, speech, and recommender systems), producing substantial reductions in parameters and latency while retaining or sometimes improving downstream performance. The literature highlights important practical trade-offs (utility vs. fairness, robustness, data availability, and teacher–student mismatch), and suggests promising directions in adaptive teacher design, rigorous uncertainty and fairness controls, and domain- and task-specific distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional — Toward Task‑Aware, Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at many levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and supports a wide range of protocols (offline teacher→student, online co‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free or privacy‑aware schemes). Empirical evidence shows KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on task awareness, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Best practice therefore treats KD as the configurable core of a broader compression pipeline that combines appropriate distillation objectives with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies) tailored to the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive signals) and across diverse protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data-free/privacy-aware schemes). When combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely enables large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Its empirical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to satisfy deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD includes a wide set of objectives and training protocols (logits/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data‑free or synthesized-data approaches). Empirical work shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance when it is matched to student capacity and data regimes and when it is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). At the same time, KD has clear limits—teacher–student mismatch, scarce or mismatched data, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and difficulty preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors—so best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline with explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Shelton

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior, representations, or relational structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and online/self- or multi-teacher protocols—are widely used across vision, language, speech, multimodal and federated settings. papers_seen.author: Rosales

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more socially or operationally suitable models. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks KD has been shown to preserve much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on constrained hardware and in privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. KD is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training, data augmentation, careful layer-matching, ensemble guidance, and hardware-aware pruning.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used Inside Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, consistently useful set of techniques for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teachers into smaller students. Empirical and methodological work across vision, language, multimodal, federated, and generative settings shows KD regularly yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and selection, and explicit mitigation of bias, distribution shift, and rare-output degradation. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated pipeline that combines representation-aware distillation with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and targeted safeguards for privacy, fairness, and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a foundational technique for compressing large models into efficient, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is effective across modalities (graphs, vision, speech, and NLP), supports privacy- and communication-constrained settings, can work without original training data, and admits algorithmic and theoretical refinements that improve robustness, interpretability, and efficiency. Combining representation-level objectives, adversarial or data-free sample generation, and task-aware layer mapping yields practical recipes for real-world compression and adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Central, Context-Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure across vision and NLP tasks and often recovers much of a teacher's performance, but it is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on what is distilled, how teachers and students are aligned, data availability, and complementary compression choices. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware component within an integrated compression pipeline yields the most robust and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields substantial latency and memory reductions while retaining much teacher performance when it is applied as part of an integrated, task- and data-aware compression pipeline. However, KD is context-sensitive: its reliability depends on choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including synthetic or teacher-generated data), and explicit measures to avoid propagating teacher artifacts or biases.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD techniques—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving protocols, and online/co-distillation schemes—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute with modest accuracy loss when applied with task-aware design. Effective use of KD typically combines careful selection of what to transfer, attention to teacher–student capacity and data regimes, and integration with complementary compression mechanisms such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfection and bias transfer, data scarcity and domain shift, capacity and optimization mismatch, and reliably distilling structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students). Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, layer-wise and many-to-many layer matching, task-aware filtering, projector-based adapters, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, and data- or privacy-constrained workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain much of teacher performance (and sometimes improve generalization) while enabling deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy; theoretical analyses offer insight into when soft labels help and when hard labels are necessary. Remaining challenges include bridging capacity gaps, dealing with mismatched architectures and modalities, operating without original data, and guaranteeing privacy under compression.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or adapts large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, generative models, and domain- or privacy-constrained settings, a diverse toolbox has been developed—soft-label supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations (e.g., pruning, layer skipping, NAS). Empirical results show that appropriately designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments, while practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and optimization design. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, privacy-and-fairness-aware protocols, and extending KD to complex generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade‑offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from larger, more expensive teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft labels, features, attention/relations, contrastive objectives) and modes (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free), and is widely used across modalities including NLP, vision, recommender systems, GANs, and reinforcement learning. Practical deployment of KD hinges on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability and augmentation, and mitigation of bias and distributional failures; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment‑aware safeguards typically yields the best trade‑offs.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a narrow training trick into a broad, practical paradigm for compressing and adapting large deep models to resource- and data-constrained deployment settings. A rich family of KD formulations — from logit matching and feature imitation to adversarial, data-free, and online schemes — together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and teacher ensembles) enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while largely preserving model quality. However, KD is not universally effective out-of-the-box: its benefits and risks depend on task characteristics, data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and deliberate choices of what and how to transfer. When practitioners treat KD as a toolkit of targeted strategies and validate choices against task constraints, it yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to the original model.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a central, practical toolkit for shrinking large neural models while preserving functionality for deployment, adaptation, and efficiency in deep learning and natural language processing. Research has developed a broad set of distillation objectives and training protocols, applied these techniques across modalities and structured tasks, and integrated KD with complementary compression methods. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance and enable new use cases (on-device inference, privacy-aware releases, multi-teacher ensembles, and task adaptation), while ongoing challenges include teacher imperfection, data heterogeneity, transferring fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees for fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or self-distillation—are combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves most teacher performance while enabling lower-latency, lower-memory, and privacy-aware deployment, but its success depends critically on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategies, and safeguards against transferred biases or degraded performance on rare phenomena; these dependencies motivate configurable, task-aware KD pipelines rather than one-size-fits-all recipes.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic, Multifaceted Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a multifaceted framework—covering logits, intermediate representations, feature maps, sample selection, and data-side interventions—KD enables deployments under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on matching the distillation signals to student capacity and task structure, and on addressing failure modes such as teacher bias and data scarcity. Combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, architecture transformations, pruning, and task-aware layer mapping) yields the best tradeoffs between compression and downstream accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD provides a flexible set of transfer targets and training protocols that, when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design, frequently yields favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful choice of distillation signals and optimization schemes. Common failure modes include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors, degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena, and fragility under domain shift and data scarcity. Treating KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—paired with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies, and privacy-aware protocols—represents current best practice for practical deployments, while several theoretical and empirical gaps motivate continued research.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. When designed as part of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline — integrating pretraining, multi-signal transfer (logits, features, relational signals), data strategies, and compatible architecture choices — KD can preserve most teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the distilled signals and data, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases or rare-case failures. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of modern model-compression toolkits, outlines concrete mechanisms by which it helps, surveys domain- and task-specific variants that address common failure modes, and summarizes actionable design principles for robust, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, datasets, and modalities. Research has advanced along several axes: designing distillation objectives (logit- and feature-based), aligning intermediate representations, performing distillation without access to original data, applying KD for domain adaptation and continual learning, and compressing or distilling generative and multimodal models. Practical deployments emphasize heterogeneous teacher-student settings, privacy and federated scenarios, and task-adaptive compression for resource-constrained inference. This review synthesizes the main methods, empirical findings, and practical considerations reported across recent work, and highlights open challenges and promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD methods span soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, data- or generator-based synthesis, and online/self- or multi-teacher protocols. Best results arise when distillation is treated as a configurable, task-aware element of an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies; persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or private data, transferred biases, degraded long-tail/rare-token behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Adaptation, Privacy, and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single compression recipe: it is a flexible family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from one set of models to another. KD enables production of compact, fast models that retain much of a larger model's performance, and it can be adapted to address domain shift, limited or private data, modality-specific constraints, and even fairness or robustness objectives. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of model deployment pipelines across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and sequential tasks) and that careful selection among KD variants (logit, feature, ensemble, online, adversarial, data-free, teacher-free, and task-aware distillation) lets practitioners balance accuracy, latency, privacy, and fairness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Guerra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When used as a configurable core—selecting appropriate transfer targets, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining with complementary compression methods and data strategies—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Its success is context dependent: task properties, data availability, teacher quality, student capacity, privacy constraints, and deployment requirements all shape which distillation protocols and auxiliary methods will work best. Responsible application therefore treats KD as the central element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal domains, a diverse set of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, data‑free or self‑distillation) have been developed. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover much of a teacher’s performance while enabling lower latency, reduced memory use, and new deployment modes; success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design of the transfer objective. Practical pipelines commonly pair KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware procedures (layer mapping, curriculum, teacher adaptation) to meet deployment constraints. Important open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift and data scarcity, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, principled automated design for heterogeneous student architectures, and privacy‑aware or data‑free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The field offers a broad toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free and synthetic-data approaches), and engineering integrations (pruning, quantization, projector or layer‑mapping choices, and architecture-aware design). Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers most teacher performance when matched to student capacity and appropriate data regimes, but it has predictable failure modes—teacher error/bias transfer, capacity and architecture mismatch, distribution shift, and degradation on rare or structured outputs—that require targeted mitigation and careful evaluation. Continued progress depends on principled choices about what and how to transfer, better data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tighter integration of KD with end-to-end compression pipelines for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible set of methods for transferring information from larger or more expressive teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD spans output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocol variants such as offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, and privacy-aware workflows. In practice KD is frequently combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and must be tailored to teacher/student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; while empirical results across modalities often show students can recover much of teacher performance, important challenges remain in handling capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias and robustness, and formal theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to satisfy deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD includes a wide set of objectives and training protocols (logits/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data‑free or synthesized-data approaches). Empirical work shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance when it is matched to student capacity and data regimes and when it is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). At the same time, KD has clear limits—teacher–student mismatch, scarce or mismatched data, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and difficulty preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors—so best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline with explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — A Position and Recommended Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows that KD can reduce inference cost, latency, and memory requirements and enable deployment under privacy, communication, and resource constraints. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, unbiased, or optimal compressed models: failures arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, transfer of teacher errors and biases, poor handling of low-frequency phenomena, and vulnerability under distribution shift or adversarial attack. Practical compression therefore treats KD as a core component within an integrated pipeline—combining representation-aware objectives, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, adversarial or synthetic-data generation for data-scarce regimes, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to realize reliable, resource-aware students.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses the capabilities of large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A variety of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, channel statistics, relational signals, or synthesized data) and protocols (offline teacher, online co-training, self-distillation, meta-learned teachers, teacher-free schemes, and data-free variants) have been developed to address deployment constraints across vision, language, speech, retrieval, detection, and generative tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation objectives and training schedules often preserve most teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but important trade-offs remain — including transferred biases, optimization and capacity gaps, data access and privacy constraints, and difficulties under distribution shift — motivating numerous methodological refinements and open research directions.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller student models. KD variants — from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate‑feature and relational objectives, multi‑teacher and online regimes, and data‑free or privacy-aware methods — routinely yield strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs when combined with task‑aware design and complementary compression primitives. However, KD’s practical success is conditional on careful choices about teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the signals to transfer, and data strategies; thus KD should be used as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines rather than as a plug‑and‑play cure.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context‑Dependent for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides a flexible set of transfer signals and training protocols that enable substantial efficiency gains when paired with appropriate data strategies and complementary compression primitives. However, KD is context‑dependent: its effectiveness hinges on teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted safeguards against bias and distributional mismatch, so it should be applied as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and multimodal domains, KD methods range from soft‑target (logit) matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure, or contrastive signals. KD is most effective when embedded in integrated compression pipelines that also leverage pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when the distillation protocol is tailored to task constraints, student capacity, and available data. Practical deployment requires addressing known failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, propagation of teacher biases or errors, and degraded performance on rare or structured outputs—and pursuing targeted remedies such as task‑aware teacher design, data synthesis or augmentation, projector layers, and joint optimization with complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Ubiquitous, but Demand-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing high-capacity models into efficient students across modalities and tasks. Empirical results across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and generative settings show KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, features, attention, contrastive objectives), the alignment between teacher and student inputs, the data used for distillation, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Carefully chosen distillation algorithms and extensions (self-supervised distillation, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, online and distributed schemes, and privacy-preserving perturbations) can mitigate common failure modes and broaden KD’s applicability in production and research settings.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of objectives (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection (or synthesis), and task‑aware design choices. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and principled methods for heterogeneous architectures and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted family of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or composite teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or generator-based approaches; it is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and pretraining to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and natural language processing shows KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance, but its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and careful choice of transfer targets and training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, pragmatic set of techniques for transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models so that compact models can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is effective across modalities and tasks when its objectives, training protocols, and data strategies are chosen to match the task, teacher–student capacities, and deployment constraints; however, KD has clear failure modes and limits that require integrated mitigation. I argue that KD should be treated as a core, configurable element of end-to-end compression pipelines rather than a standalone, one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource and privacy constraints, and sometimes improve robustness or task adaptation. A diverse toolkit has been developed—logit/soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and generative data-free techniques, multi-teacher and online schemes, and selective or meta-learned teaching—and empirical and theoretical work clarifies when and why these choices succeed or fail. Practical deployment requires matching the distilled signal to student capacity and task constraints, handling data- or architecture-mismatch, and explicitly addressing bias and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and supports diverse training protocols (offline, online/self, multi‑teacher, and data‑free or privacy‑aware variants). Across vision, speech, graph, 3D detection, and language tasks, KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade‑offs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate transfer targets, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is not a universal cure: limitations such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and bias transfer require targeted mitigations and careful evaluation. Treating KD as a configurable core element within integrated compression pipelines yields the most reliable path to deployable, high‑performing compact models.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the task, data regime, and student capacity, KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance and enables deployment under compute, latency, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and loss of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically effective approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving most of a teacher's performance—but it is context dependent, requiring careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, privacy, and deployment constraints. Treated as the configurable core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware data strategies), KD enables deployable models for latency- and resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings; however, practitioners must explicitly address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, low-frequency errors, and propagated biases.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied, pragmatic toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks the field has developed a diverse taxonomy of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational/contrastive structure), training protocols (offline, online/self, multi-teacher, data‑free), and integrations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost, but practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling limited or mismatched data, and mitigating risks such as transferred biases, privacy leakage, and degraded rare-output behavior.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broadly applicable toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more interpretable models from large teacher networks. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, and synthetic data, and they commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and automated architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most teacher performance while substantially reducing latency and memory, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and task-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates via soft-label (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial or generative synthesis of data, and many hybrid protocols. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task- and data-specific constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and careful objective design. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a central, configurable component of an integrated compression strategy rather than a one-shot solution.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. A diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, many-to-many layer mappings, projector-based feature transforms, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or adversarial sample synthesis — enables large reductions in parameters and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability and privacy, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Remaining research challenges include principled theory for objective selection, reliable transfer under data heterogeneity and privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher–student matching for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Configurable First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. papers_seen.author: Burgess

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Component of Practical Model Compression

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied collection of techniques for transferring information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool that Requires Task-Aware, Complementary Engineering

papers_seen.author: Bartlett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, broadly applicable family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teacher models. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains shows that KD—particularly when combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when guided by task‑aware objectives and data strategies—regularly yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs. However, KD is context dependent: its effectiveness hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and nature of distillation data, and explicit mitigations for bias, robustness, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a stand‑alone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Work in this area spans logit matching, representation-level objectives, data-free and few-shot regimes, multi-/online-teacher schemes, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling large reductions in memory and compute, but limitations remain around optimization, data availability, and the preservation or mitigation of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models using targets ranging from soft logits to intermediate representations and relational signals. Across vision, language, multimodal, and speech tasks, KD combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation or synthetic-data generation) enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical results show distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can sometimes match or exceed teachers when distillation is carefully designed. Important open problems include teacher–student capacity mismatch, optimization and belief-matching limits, distribution shift and domain adaptation, preserving rare-token/low-frequency behavior, and avoiding transfer of teacher biases. This synthesis summarizes mechanisms, practical variants, representative empirical patterns, and recommended directions for research and deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mccormick
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When designed with attention to which signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, and distillation-data strategies, and when combined with complementary compression primitives, KD routinely yields favorable tradeoffs between efficiency and performance across modalities. However, KD is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare‑token behavior, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional shift. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware element of integrated compression pipelines — rather than a turnkey replacement for other techniques — produces the most reproducible deployments and points to principled research directions for robust, privacy‑aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Byrd

papers_seen.author: Kramer

papers_seen.author: Robertson

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. Remaining gaps include principled layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, robust distillation under limited or private data, preservation of long‑tail/low‑frequency behaviors, and theoretical understanding of when particular teacher signals are necessary.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez

papers_seen.author: Colon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance

papers_seen.author: Padilla
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information at multiple levels (soft logits, internal features, attention and relational structure) and are effective across vision, language, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and preparation, and the choice and timing of transfer objectives. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be treated as a configurable component embedded in an integrated pipeline that includes complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), data and curriculum strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and rare-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
